parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
String of conditions to filter resources by.
Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description:
Set the page token to start from.
Use page tokens to page through list results or list specific pages.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Set the page size to limit the number of results returned.
Default: 100. Max: 500.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action to be executed with a request. Not supported for all endpoints.

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: List of fields to return (all fields are returned by default).

parameters.name: traverse
parameters.description: Get data from any child namespaces as well.

parameters.name: sort.path
parameters.description: Field to sort objects by, for example, meta.name.

parameters.name: sort.order
parameters.description: Sort order. Default: ASC.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
Return the number of objects matching the given list parameters.
If count is set to true, the response is a CountResponse.
Can be used together with filter and traverse.

parameters.name: group.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this field.
If there are multiple fields then the objects are grouped
based on the uniqueness of all fields.
Supports composite paths.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: group.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description:
Return the UUID of each object in each group as specified by
aggregation_paths.

parameters.name: group.unique_count_paths
parameters.description:
List of fields for which we want the unique count.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: group.unique_value_paths
parameters.description:
List of fields for which we want the unique values.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: ci_run_uuid
parameters.description: Only return objects from PR scans that match this context id.

parameters.name: page_id
parameters.description: Page ID to retrieve.

parameters.name: group_by_time.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this time field,
for example, meta.create_time.

parameters.name: group_by_time.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description: Return the UUIDs of the objects in each group.

parameters.name: group_by_time.interval
parameters.description: Interval unit by which the objects should be grouped.

parameters.name: group_by_time.group_size
parameters.description:
Size of the time interval to group the objects by,
for example, to group objects by 2-week intervals, set interval
to GROUP_BY_TIME_INTERVAL_WEEK and group_size to 2.

parameters.name: group_by_time.start_time
parameters.description:
Beginning of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the beginning of time.

parameters.name: group_by_time.end_time
parameters.description:
End of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the current time.

parameters.name: group_by_time.mode
parameters.description:
The mode determines how the matching objects are counted
in the produced time-series. Values allowed are:
count (default) : is the number of items matching in every interval.
sum: is the total number of items matching since the beginning of the
aggregation time.

parameters.name: group_by_time.aggregation_value_field
parameters.description:
The aggregation_field is a field on the matched objects that we want to
perform some operation in each interval (example : min, max, avg)

parameters.name: group_by_time.aggregation_operator
parameters.description:
The aggreation_operator is the operator that we should use for the
aggregation. Allowed values are: min, max, sum, avg

parameters.name: disable_pagination
parameters.description:
If true, the results will not be paginated and
only the first page will be returned. The order
of the results is not guaranteed.

parameters.name: list_parameters.filter
parameters.description:
String of conditions to filter resources by.
Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_token
parameters.description:
Set the page token to start from.
Use page tokens to page through list results or list specific pages.

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_size
parameters.description:
Set the page size to limit the number of results returned.
Default: 100. Max: 500.

parameters.name: list_parameters.action
parameters.description: Action to be executed with a request. Not supported for all endpoints.

parameters.name: list_parameters.mask
parameters.description: List of fields to return (all fields are returned by default).

parameters.name: list_parameters.traverse
parameters.description: Get data from any child namespaces as well.

parameters.name: list_parameters.sort.path
parameters.description: Field to sort objects by, for example, meta.name.

parameters.name: list_parameters.sort.order
parameters.description: Sort order. Default: ASC.

parameters.name: list_parameters.count
parameters.description:
Return the number of objects matching the given list parameters.
If count is set to true, the response is a CountResponse.
Can be used together with filter and traverse.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this field.
If there are multiple fields then the objects are grouped
based on the uniqueness of all fields.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description:

aggregation_paths.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.unique_count_paths

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.unique_value_paths
parameters.description:

parameters.description: Only return objects from PR scans that match this context id.

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_id
parameters.description: Page ID to retrieve.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this time field,

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description: Return the UUIDs of the objects in each group.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.interval
parameters.description: Interval unit by which the objects should be grouped.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.group_size
parameters.description:
Size of the time interval to group the objects by,
for example, to group objects by 2-week intervals, set interval
to GROUP_BY_TIME_INTERVAL_WEEK and group_size to 2.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.start_time
parameters.description:
Beginning of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the beginning of time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.end_time
parameters.description:
End of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the current time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.mode
parameters.description:
The mode determines how the matching objects are counted
in the produced time-series. Values allowed are:
count (default) : is the number of items matching in every interval.
sum: is the total number of items matching since the beginning of the
aggregation time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_value_field
parameters.description:
The aggregation_field is a field on the matched objects that we want to
perform some operation in each interval (example : min, max, avg)

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_operator
parameters.description:
The aggreation_operator is the operator that we should use for the
aggregation. Allowed values are: min, max, sum, avg

parameters.name: list_parameters.disable_pagination
parameters.description:
If true, the results will not be paginated and
only the first page will be returned. The order
of the results is not guaranteed.

String of conditions to filter resources by.
Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_token
parameters.description:
Set the page token to start from.
Use page tokens to page through list results or list specific pages.

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_size
parameters.description:
Set the page size to limit the number of results returned.
Default: 100. Max: 500.

parameters.name: list_parameters.action
parameters.description: Action to be executed with a request. Not supported for all endpoints.

parameters.name: list_parameters.mask
parameters.description: List of fields to return (all fields are returned by default).

parameters.name: list_parameters.traverse
parameters.description: Get data from any child namespaces as well.

parameters.name: list_parameters.sort.path
parameters.description: Field to sort objects by, for example, meta.name.

parameters.name: list_parameters.sort.order
parameters.description: Sort order. Default: ASC.

parameters.name: list_parameters.count
parameters.description:
Return the number of objects matching the given list parameters.
If count is set to true, the response is a CountResponse.
Can be used together with filter and traverse.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this field.
If there are multiple fields then the objects are grouped
based on the uniqueness of all fields.
Supports composite paths.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description:
Return the UUID of each object in each group as specified by
aggregation_paths.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.unique_count_paths
parameters.description:
List of fields for which we want the unique count.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.unique_value_paths
parameters.description:
List of fields for which we want the unique values.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: list_parameters.ci_run_uuid
parameters.description: Only return objects from PR scans that match this context id.

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_id
parameters.description: Page ID to retrieve.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this time field,
for example, meta.create_time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description: Return the UUIDs of the objects in each group.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.interval
parameters.description: Interval unit by which the objects should be grouped.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.group_size
parameters.description:
Size of the time interval to group the objects by,
for example, to group objects by 2-week intervals, set interval
to GROUP_BY_TIME_INTERVAL_WEEK and group_size to 2.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.start_time
parameters.description:
Beginning of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the beginning of time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.end_time
parameters.description:
End of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the current time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.mode
parameters.description:
The mode determines how the matching objects are counted
in the produced time-series. Values allowed are:
count (default) : is the number of items matching in every interval.
sum: is the total number of items matching since the beginning of the
aggregation time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_value_field
parameters.description:
The aggregation_field is a field on the matched objects that we want to
perform some operation in each interval (example : min, max, avg)

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_operator
parameters.description:
The aggreation_operator is the operator that we should use for the
aggregation. Allowed values are: min, max, sum, avg

parameters.name: list_parameters.disable_pagination
parameters.description:
If true, the results will not be paginated and
only the first page will be returned. The order
of the results is not guaranteed.

parameters.name: list_parameters.filter
parameters.description:
String of conditions to filter resources by.
Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_token
parameters.description:
Set the page token to start from.
Use page tokens to page through list results or list specific pages.

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_size
parameters.description:
Set the page size to limit the number of results returned.
Default: 100. Max: 500.

parameters.name: list_parameters.action
parameters.description: Action to be executed with a request. Not supported for all endpoints.

parameters.name: list_parameters.mask
parameters.description: List of fields to return (all fields are returned by default).

parameters.name: list_parameters.traverse
parameters.description: Get data from any child namespaces as well.

parameters.name: list_parameters.sort.path
parameters.description: Field to sort objects by, for example, meta.name.

parameters.name: list_parameters.sort.order
parameters.description: Sort order. Default: ASC.

parameters.name: list_parameters.count
parameters.description:
Return the number of objects matching the given list parameters.
If count is set to true, the response is a CountResponse.
Can be used together with filter and traverse.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this field.
If there are multiple fields then the objects are grouped
based on the uniqueness of all fields.
Supports composite paths.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description:
Return the UUID of each object in each group as specified by
aggregation_paths.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.unique_count_paths
parameters.description:
List of fields for which we want the unique count.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group.unique_value_paths
parameters.description:
List of fields for which we want the unique values.
Supports arrays and maps.

parameters.name: list_parameters.ci_run_uuid
parameters.description: Only return objects from PR scans that match this context id.

parameters.name: list_parameters.page_id
parameters.description: Page ID to retrieve.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_paths
parameters.description:
Group the objects based on this time field,
for example, meta.create_time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.show_aggregation_uuids
parameters.description: Return the UUIDs of the objects in each group.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.interval
parameters.description: Interval unit by which the objects should be grouped.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.group_size
parameters.description:
Size of the time interval to group the objects by,
for example, to group objects by 2-week intervals, set interval
to GROUP_BY_TIME_INTERVAL_WEEK and group_size to 2.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.start_time
parameters.description:
Beginning of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the beginning of time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.end_time
parameters.description:
End of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the current time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.mode
parameters.description:
The mode determines how the matching objects are counted
in the produced time-series. Values allowed are:
count (default) : is the number of items matching in every interval.
sum: is the total number of items matching since the beginning of the
aggregation time.

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_value_field
parameters.description:
The aggregation_field is a field on the matched objects that we want to
perform some operation in each interval (example : min, max, avg)

parameters.name: list_parameters.group_by_time.aggregation_operator
parameters.description:
The aggreation_operator is the operator that we should use for the
aggregation. Allowed values are: min, max, sum, avg

parameters.name: list_parameters.disable_pagination
parameters.description:
If true, the results will not be paginated and
only the first page will be returned. The order
of the results is not guaranteed.

context.description:

by any non-FIXED outcome (STILL_PRESENT, UNKNOWN, agent error).

AISASTScanCacheScanOutcome.description:
ScanOutcome represents the result of scanning a segment or file.

 - SCAN_OUTCOME_UNSPECIFIED: No outcome has been set.
 - SCAN_OUTCOME_SUCCESS: Segment was scanned successfully; results (if any) are in LinterResult.
 - SCAN_OUTCOME_SKIPPED: Segment was skipped as not interesting or trivial.
 - SCAN_OUTCOME_FAILED: LLM call or post-processing failed for this segment.
 - SCAN_OUTCOME_OUT_OF_SCOPE: Segment was excluded by include/exclude path rules.
 - SCAN_OUTCOME_IN_PROGRESS: File is currently owned by an active scan attempt.

approach as repoindexer/indexer.go calculateHash.

AISASTScanCacheServiceCreateAISASTScanCa.description:
AISASTScanCache tracks scan outcomes at file-level granularity for AI SAST
incremental scanning. Each document contains the segments for a single
file, enabling efficient bulk reads and writes against MongoDB. When the
outcome changes (e.g. a previously failed file is retried successfully),
the existing cache entry is updated in place.

This is a cache: LinterResults remain the authoritative finding records.
If the cache is lost, the system falls back to a full scan.

ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQueryServi.description:
ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuery computes, on demand, how the vulnerability
findings of a scanned container image's base image would change if the base
were moved to each of its available update options (refreshed, next, latest).
It is a computed query in the style of DashboardSummaryQuery: the response is
derived live from existing Finding and PackageVersion records and is never
persisted, so it cannot go stale as findings are recomputed.

ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQue.description:
A reachability bucket to page (the reachability view).

 - REACHABILITY_BUCKET_UNSPECIFIED: The reachability bucket was not set.
 - REACHABILITY_BUCKET_REACHABLE: Findings on dependencies reachable in the app image.
 - REACHABILITY_BUCKET_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE: Findings on dependencies that may be reachable in the app image.
 - REACHABILITY_BUCKET_UNREACHABLE: Findings on dependencies not reachable in the app image.

Which side of the diff to page: fixed and introduced are separate lists.

 - RECORD_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: The kind was not set.
 - RECORD_KIND_FIXED: Findings present on the current base but gone on the candidate (fixed).
 - RECORD_KIND_INTRODUCED: Findings absent on the current base but present on the candidate.

ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQue.description:
ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQuery pages through the full fixed or
introduced finding list for a single update option and a single bucket (one
severity or one reachability bucket), using the standard ListParameters
pagination contract. It backs each per-bucket "View more" in the impact UI.
The impact query above returns only the top-N inline records per bucket; this
query is the drill-down for the complete per-bucket, per-kind set.

Which update option's diff to page through.

 - UPDATE_OPTION_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: The update option was not set.
 - UPDATE_OPTION_KIND_REFRESHED: The refreshed base (update_options.refreshed).
 - UPDATE_OPTION_KIND_NEXT: The next base (update_options.next_version).
 - UPDATE_OPTION_KIND_LATEST: The latest base (update_options.latest_version).

ApplicationType represents the type of the application.

 - APPLICATION_TYPE_CLI: CLI application type.
It is typically set when container image does not have any exposed ports.
 - APPLICATION_TYPE_SERVER: Server application type.
It is typically set when container image has exposed ports.

ContainerProfileDetailsProfileType.description:
ProfileType represents the type of the profile.

 - PROFILE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified profile type.
 - PROFILE_TYPE_BASIC: Basic profile type.
It Indicates that a container image was profiled using a built in profiling mechanism.
 - PROFILE_TYPE_INSTRUMENTED: Instrumented profile type.
It Indicates that a container image was profiled using an instrumented profiling mechanism.

ContainerProfileErrorContainerProfileSta.description:
ContainerProfileStatus indicates the result of profiling a container image.

 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED indicates that the container profile
status has not been set or is unknown.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND indicates that the Mint toolkit
plugin required for profiling the container image was not found.
This typically occurs when the profiling environment is misconfigured
or the required Mint toolkit plugin is not installed.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_TIMEOUT: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_TIMEOUT indicates that the profiling operation
exceeded the allowed time limit.
This typically occurs for complex container images that require
extensive processing time or when system resources are constrained.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE indicates that the container
image exceeds the maximum allowed size for profiling.
This typically occurs when the uncompressed container image size
exceeds the system's configured size limit for profiling operations.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_IMAGE_NOT_RUNNABLE: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_IMAGE_NOT_RUNNABLE indicates that the container
image cannot be executed without additional configuration.
This typically occurs when the container image requires specific
environment variables, volumes, network configuration, or entrypoint
arguments that were not provided during the profiling attempt.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_MINT_PLUGIN_ERROR: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_MINT_PLUGIN_ERROR indicates that the Mint plugin
encountered an error while profiling the container image.
This typically occurs when the Mint plugin encounters an unexpected
condition, such as incompatible image format, corrupted layers, or
internal plugin failures during the profiling process.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_ARTIFACTS_NOT_FOUND: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_ARTIFACTS_NOT_FOUND indicates that the expected
profiling artifacts were not found after the profiling operation completed.
This typically occurs when the profiling process runs successfully but
fails to produce or persist the expected output artifacts, possibly due
to storage issues or unexpected container behavior during profiling.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR indicates that an internal error occurred while profiling the container image.
This typically occurs when an unexpected error occurs during the profiling process,
such as a programming error or an unexpected system failure.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_PLUGIN_SETUP: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_PLUGIN_SETUP indicates that an error occurred while setting up the Mint toolkit plugin.
This typically occurs when there is an error in setting up the Mint toolkit plugin.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_PROFILE_LOAD: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_PROFILE_LOAD indicates that the profiling data was not found or corrupted.
Indicates that the profiling is successfully completed but the profiling data was not found or corrupted.
It can happen if the creport.json file is not found or corrupted.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_MINT_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_MINT_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE indicates that the Mint version is incompatible with the profiling requirements.
This typically occurs when the Mint version is not compatible with the profiling requirements.
 - CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_IMAGE_TYPE_BASE: CONTAINER_PROFILE_STATUS_IMAGE_TYPE_BASE indicates that the container
image was identified as a base image (OS distribution or language runtime)
and dynamic profiling was skipped because base images contain no
application code to profile.

reference name.

ContributorIdentityMappingServiceCreateC.description:
ContributorIdentityMapping links a SCM login to one or more normalized commit emails for a tenant.
Data is populated from SCM APIs (e.g. App based scans or PAT-backed reports) and used to deduplicate contributors across emails.

Deterministic canonical_email (persisted in spec.canonical_email, applied on create/update only):
 1. Normalize every associated email: trim ASCII whitespace and lowercase (same rules as contributor aggregation).
 2. Deduplicate, then sort lexicographically before persisting associated_emails.
 3. If any email is a GitHub noreply address for this login (see github.com docs: USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com
    or ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com), pick the lexicographically smallest matching noreply address.
 4. Otherwise use the lexicographically smallest normalized email.

Aggregation and other readers must use spec.canonical_email as stored;
they must not re-derive a different "first" email from scan order.

DependencyImportedType.description:
ImportedType is the state of import.

 - IMPORTED_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: UNSPECIFIED is the default state. This state denotes that imported
dependency analysis has not been run yet for this dependency.
 - IMPORTED_TYPE_IN_SOURCE: IN_SOURCE means the imported dependency analysis succeeded and found
that the dependency is imported in source.
 - IMPORTED_TYPE_NOT_IN_SOURCE: NOT_IN_SOURCE means the imported dependency analysis succeeded and
found that the dependency is not imported in source.
 - IMPORTED_TYPE_PHANTOM: PHANTOM means the imported dependency analysis succeeded and found that
the dependency is imported only in the source (a phantom dependency).
 - IMPORTED_TYPE_SEGMENT_MATCH: Dependency was discovered through code segment match.
 - IMPORTED_TYPE_INSTALLED_IN_USE: Dependency was discovered through installed dependencies and it is in use.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project to which the dependency belongs.

package_name.description:
Qualified dependency package name. Does not include the version.
For example, for go://package@v1.2.3 this is set to "go://package".

package_version_uuid.description: the UUID of the dependency package version object.

unresolved_version.description: Unresolved dependency package version string. For example, "v2.0.0".

resolved_version.description: Resolved dependency package version. For example, "v2.0.0".

direct.description: True if this is a direct dependency.

pinned.description:
Set to true of the dependency is fixed to a specific version by a
manifest file (intent).

For example, in package.json, "lodash": "4.17.21" is pinned while
"lodash": "^4.0.0" is not (it's a range, "any 4.x").

reachable.description: True if the dependency is reachable.

utilization.description:
Percent of the dependency used based on the call graph. Implementation
pending.

namespace.description: Namespace to which the dependency package version object belongs.

parent_version_name.description:
Fully qualified name of the direct parent of the dependency. For example,
go://package@v1.2.3.

repo_name.description: Name of the repository to which the dependency belongs.

internal.description:
True if the dependency is in the same namespace or, if the
namespace is oss, in the same project as the importer.

parent_count.description: Total number of direct parents in dependency graph.

callgraph_available.description: True if the call graph is available.

last_commit.description: Date that the dependency was last modified.
last_commit.x-endor-name: Date of Last Commit in Dependency Version

abstract.description:
True if the dependency is an abstract dependency, such as a secondary Pom
file.

missing.description: True if the package version is missing for this dependency.

approximation.description:
True if this is an approximate dependency based on unresolved package
dependencies.

public.description: True if the dependency is public.

project_paths.description:
List of all project paths to this dependency from the root package
version (importer).

vendored.description: True if the dependency is a vendored dependency.

discovery_type.description: Indicates how the dependency was discovered.

patched.description: Indicates whether the dependency version was patched or not.

container_data.description: Container image metadata for the dependency if applicable.

purl.description: The purl for the dependency package version.

eol_timestamp.description: End of life timestamp for the dependency package version.

eol.description: Indicates whether the dependency is end of life.

declared_licenses.description: Declared license information for the dependency.

discovered_licenses.description: Discovered license information for the dependency.

locked.description:
Set to true if the dependency is fixed to a specific version by a
lock file at install time (outcome).

If a dependency is locked, but not pinned, it could drift if the
lock file is regenerated (for example, by 'npm update').

The public package this private dependency was forked from, so its
vulnerabilities can be attributed to the fork. Empty means the resolver
has not run yet; "N/A" means it ran and found no upstream.

forked.description:
Set to true if the dependency is a downstream fork of a public dependency.
True exactly when upstream_reference names a package, so both fields are
written together.

native_scope.description:

EndorIgnoreEntryServiceCreateEndorIgnore.description:
Represents a single entry in the ignore file.

EndorIgnoreEntry objects are created by the endorctl client after
reading and processing the ignore file during the git scan,
and then applied to the findings during the analytics scan.

The ignore file is either a raw list of vulnerability ids
(one per line), or a YAML file that contains a list of ignore entries,
each identifying one or more findings in a repository version.
The file is formatted manually or via the endorctl ignore command.

Each entry must specify at least the finding name or the vulnerability ID.
The more fields you provide, the more specific the ignore entry is.
I.e. if you only provide the finding name and there are multiple
findings with the same name in the same repository version,
the ignore entry is applied to all of them.
Use the endorctl ignore --finding-uuid option to automatically populate
all fields of the ignore entry based on a given finding.

FunctionSummaryHashesQueryServiceCreateF.description:
FunctionSummaryHashesQuery reports which of the given segment hashes are
missing a usable function summary, of any status, at the given prompt
version or newer. Unlike FunctionSummaryQuery, which returns full summary
content and only matches usable ('ok') summaries for search consumers,
this checks bare existence so a client can skip re-summarizing a segment
already tombstoned as trivial or failed.

aggregation_paths.description:
Group the objects based on this time field,
for example, meta.create_time.

show_aggregation_uuids.description: Return the UUIDs of the objects in each group.

interval.description: Interval unit by which the objects should be grouped.

group_size.description:
Size of the time interval to group the objects by,
for example, to group objects by 2-week intervals, set interval
to GROUP_BY_TIME_INTERVAL_WEEK and group_size to 2.

start_time.description:
Beginning of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the beginning of time.

end_time.description:
End of the time period to group objects.
Defaults to the current time.

mode.description:
The mode determines how the matching objects are counted
in the produced time-series. Values allowed are:
count (default) : is the number of items matching in every interval.
sum: is the total number of items matching since the beginning of the
aggregation time.

aggregation_value_field.title:
The aggregation_field is a field on the matched objects that we want to
perform some operation in each interval (example : min, max, avg)

aggregation_operator.title:
The aggreation_operator is the operator that we should use for the
aggregation. Allowed values are: min, max, sum, avg

Optional version ranges. A package version matches if it falls within any of these ranges.
If both version_ranges and exact_versions are empty, all versions of the package are excepted.

exact_versions.description: Optional list of exact version strings to except.

Exception defines an allowlist rule for a specific package and optional version constraints.
If any exception matches the request, all checks are skipped immediately.

reasons.description: Firewall reasons that trigger this rule. Empty matches all reasons.

on_actions.description: Firewall actions that trigger this rule. Empty matches all actions.

end.description: Exclusive upper bound (e.g. "2.0.0"). Omit to match to the end.

VersionRange defines an inclusive lower bound and an exclusive upper bound for a version range.
Either boundary may be omitted.

version.description: Version string that was suppressed from the metadata response.

This is the full text of the license that will be used instead of the original.

file_locations.description:
The file locations where the license was found in the source code.
This helps identify where the original license was located.

spdx_ids.description: The SPDX IDs of the license (e.g., ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]).

spdx_expr.description: The SPDX expression of the license (e.g., "MIT OR Apache-2.0").

url.description: The URL link to the license details (if available).

copyrights.description: The copyrights within the license text.

type.description:
License classification (based on licenseclassifier by Google).
Examples: "notice", "reciprocal", "permissive", "restricted", etc.

source.description:
Source of the original license (e.g., "code", "package_manager", "declared").
This helps identify which original license this override corresponds to.

original_hash.description:
Hash of the original license from PackageLicenseInfo.hash (if overriding existing license).
This is the hash that maps to the key in PackageLicense.spec.license_text map.
For new licenses added by user, this will be empty (the hash is calculated from license_text and used as the map key).

file_locations.description: The file locations where the notice was found in the source code.

at the package version level. Edits made at this level apply across all projects in the namespace
that use the same package version.
The package version UUID is stored in spec.package_version_uuid.

identifier.description:
Stable identifier/key for this copyright (file path from PackageLicense.spec.copyrights map or generated UUID for new copyrights).
This identifier is used as the key in copyright_overrides and deselected_copyrights maps.
For copyrights from PackageLicense: uses the file path key from PackageLicense.spec.copyrights map.
For new copyrights added by user: uses generated UUID prefixed with "new-".
To determine if a copyright is new: check if identifier starts with "new-" or does not exist in original PackageLicense.

selected.description:
Whether this copyright is selected for inclusion in notice file.
true = selected (will be included), false = deselected (will be excluded).
Defaults to true if not present in deselected_copyrights map.

is_edited.description:
Whether this copyright has been edited/overridden.
true = copyright text has been modified from original, false = using original copyright text.
Can be derived by checking if identifier exists in copyright_overrides map.

copyright_text.description:
The copyright text (from override if edited, otherwise from original).
This is the actual copyright text that will be used.

file_locations.description: File locations where the copyright was found (from override if edited, otherwise from original).

resolved_namespace.description: Origin of the effective value for this entry.

PackageLicenseQueryMergedCopyrightEntry.description: MergedCopyrightEntry represents a single copyright with override and selection state.

identifier.description:
Stable identifier for this license (hash calculated from normalized license text).
This identifier is used as the key in license_overrides and deselected_licenses maps.
For licenses from PackageLicense: uses PackageLicenseInfo.hash.
For new licenses added by user: hash is calculated from license_text using SHA256(MakeLicenseKey(normalized_text)).
To determine if a license is new: check if identifier does not exist in original PackageLicense.

selected.description:
Whether this license is selected for inclusion in notice file.
true = selected (will be included), false = deselected (will be excluded).
Defaults to true if not present in deselected_licenses map.

is_edited.description:
Whether this license has been edited/overridden.
true = license text has been modified from original, false = using original license text.
Can be derived by checking if identifier exists in license_overrides map.

source.description:
Source of the original license (e.g., "code", "package_manager", "declared").
Helps identify which category the license belongs to.

license_text.description: Effective license text resolved after applying propagation across the namespace chain.

resolved_namespace.description:
Origin of the effective value for this entry.
If no override is applied, resolved_namespace will typically be "oss" and
resolved_override_uuid will be empty.

file_locations.description: File locations where the license was found (from override if edited, otherwise from original).

 - SCOPE_COMPILE: Dependency is required at compile time.

 - SCOPE_TEST: Dependency is not required at runtime and is only used for test
purposes.

ecosystems.

 - SCOPE_IMPORT: Dependency is imported via pom/abstract dependency.

If disable_enforcement is set the policy will just log the result
and not enforce an action. This allows debugging and observation
of the system.

For policy templates, this is used as the default value but
it can be changed.

Additional tags for the finding that is created.
For policy templates, this is used as the default value but
it can be changed.

categories.description:
List of categories that capture the use cases the finding fits in.
For policy templates, this is used as the default value but
it can be changed.

summary.description:
Summary of the finding that is created.
For policy templates this is used as the default value but
it can be changed to any free form string.

explanation.description:
Explanation provides information about the reason this is considered
noteworthy. For policy templates this is used as the default value but
it can be changed to any free form string.

remediation.description:
Remediation instructions.
For policy templates this is used as the default value but
it can be changed to any free form string.

external_name.description:
External finding name.
For policy templates this is used as the default value but
it can be changed to any free form string.

meta_tags.description: Additional meta tags for the finding that is created.

target_kind.description:
Repository, RepositoryVersion, or PackageVersion.
This is usually the same as the finding parent kind.

PolicyPolicyType.description:
- POLICY_TYPE_ADMISSION: POLICY_TYPE_ADMISSION will admit/reject pipeline runs.
Admission policies operate on Findings and are run during
a CI/CD pipeline. They may return data such as the uuids
of findings that violate the policy.
 - POLICY_TYPE_NOTIFICATION: POLICY_TYPE_NOTIFICATION is for policies that generate notifications.
 - POLICY_TYPE_ML_FINDING: ML finding policies enable or disable algorithmic findings.
Note that there is no input data for these policies,
they always return output, and the allowed value is ignored.
 - POLICY_TYPE_SYSTEM_FINDING: A system finding policy is created from a system policy
template. It processes data and creates new findings.
System finding policies are run together with user and
ML (a.k.a. algorithmic) findings.
System finding policies can only be enabled, disabled, and
edited. They cannot be created or deleted.
 - POLICY_TYPE_USER_FINDING: A user finding policy is created from scratch or from a customer
policy template. It processes data and creates new findings.
User finding policies are run together with system and
ML (a.k.a. algorithmic) findings.
User finding policies can be created, enabled, disabled, edited,
and deleted.
 - POLICY_TYPE_EXCEPTION: An exception policy identifies findings which should be
excluded from admission and notification policies. It is
created from scratch or from an exception policy template.
 - POLICY_TYPE_REMEDIATION: A remediation policy identifies findings which should be
remediated. It is created from scratch or from a remediation
policy template.

PullRequestSecurityReviewResultInfoChang.description:
ChangeDescription provides a detailed explanation of specific changes made within a file.
Used to track and document individual modifications for better understanding of the changes.

ChangeKind indicates the type of modification made to a code element (file, function, or snippet)
within the pull request. This helps track whether items are newly added, modified, or removed.

 - CHANGE_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: Default state when the change type is unknown
 - CHANGE_KIND_NEW: Indicates a newly added element
 - CHANGE_KIND_MODIFIED: Indicates an existing element that was modified
 - CHANGE_KIND_REMOVED: Indicates an element that was removed

PullRequestSecurityReviewResultInfoSecur.description:
SecurityRelevantFunction represents a function or method that performs security-sensitive operations.
or requires special security consideration during review.

SecurityCategory represents the different categories of security aspects that can be evaluated.

 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED: Default when category is unknown
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_DEPENDENCY: Integration of external code, packages, and frameworks
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_ACCESS_CONTROL: Authentication, authorization mechanisms and session management
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_API_ENDPOINT: API and service entry points
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_DATABASE: Database architecture and security
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_CRYPTOGRAPHIC: Cryptographic systems and implementations
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_PAYMENT_PROCESSING: Payment processing and financial systems
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_MEMORY_PROTECTION: Memory management and protection
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_PII_DATA_HANDLING: Processing of PII and sensitive information
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_INPUT_VALIDATION: Input validation and processing security
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_INFRASTRUCTURE: Infrastructure security
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_CI_CD: CI/CD pipeline security
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_CONFIGURATION: Application and infrastructure configuration
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_NETWORK: Network security and communication protocols
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_AI: AI/LLM integration security
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_IMPROVEMENT: Improvement to the security posture
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_VULNERABILITY: Vulnerability found in the code
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CATEGORY_BUG: Bug found in the code

SecurityReviewConfidenceLevel represents the confidence level in the security assessment.

 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED: Default confidence level when confidence is unknown
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_LOW: Low confidence level
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_MEDIUM: Medium confidence level
 - SECURITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_HIGH: High confidence level

Level represents the severity or importance level of a security aspect or finding
Used to prioritize security concerns and determine the urgency of required actions.

 - SECURITY_SEVERITY_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED: Default level when severity is unknown
 - SECURITY_SEVERITY_LEVEL_LOW: Minor security concerns with minimal impact
 - SECURITY_SEVERITY_LEVEL_MEDIUM: Moderate security concerns that should be addressed
 - SECURITY_SEVERITY_LEVEL_HIGH: Significant security concerns requiring prompt attention
 - SECURITY_SEVERITY_LEVEL_CRITICAL: Critical security issues that need immediate remediation

ResolutionStatusStatusError.description:
StatusError is the type of issue discovered.

 - STATUS_ERROR_MANIFEST_LOAD: MANIFEST_LOAD indicates that the system is unable to find the manifest of
the language (pom.xml, packages.json, etc). This status error is only
used for unresolved dependencies.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The callgraph will not be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version is marked as failed and
endorctl will log an error.

For OSS packages:
When it happens and if the package version is in the OSS namespace, the
package version will not be scanned anymore. When it happens, the scan of
the package version is marked as failed and endorctl will log an error.
 - STATUS_ERROR_MANIFEST_PARSE: MANIFEST_PARSE indicates that the system failed to parse the manifest.
This status error is only used for unresolved dependencies.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The callgraph will be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version is marked as failed and
endorctl will log an error.

For OSS packages:
When it happens and if the package version is in the OSS namespace, the
package version will not be scanned anymore. When it happens, the scan of
the package version is marked as failed and endorctl will log an error.
 - STATUS_ERROR_MANIFEST_EMPTY: MANIFEST_EMPTY indicates that the system failed to find
any dependencies and is returning empty results on purpose.
DEPRECATED: use STATUS_ERROR_MANIFEST_PARSE instead.
 - STATUS_ERROR_DEPENDENCY: DEPENDENCY indicates that the system failed to resolve a dependency.
Usually this happens when a manifest contains bad associations of
dependencies and versions. This status error is only used for resolved
dependencies.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The callgraph will be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version is marked as failed and
endorctl will log an error.

For OSS packages:
When it happens and if the package version is in the OSS namespace, the
package version will not be scanned anymore. When it happens, the scan of
the package version is marked as failed and endorctl will log an error.
 - STATUS_ERROR_CALL_GRAPH: CALL_GRAPH indicates that the system failed to construct the call graph.
This status error is only used for callgraph computation.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The callgraph will not be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will not be marked as
failed, only a warning log will be emitted by the system.

For OSS packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will not be marked as
failed, only a warning log will be emitted by the system.
 - STATUS_ERROR_MISSING_ARTIFACT: MISSING_ARTIFACT indicates that the system failed to compute the
callgraph because the package is not built. This status error is only
used for callgraph computation.

For OSS packages:
When it happens, the system will try to build the package and the
computation of the callgraph will be launched again.

It should be noted that we should never have this state set in a package
version. This is a transient state only used by the system. This state
can not happen for tenant packages, we always expect that tenant packages
will be built for us.
 - STATUS_ERROR_BUILD: BUILD indicates that the plugin failed to build the package version.
This status error is only used for unresolved dependencies.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The callgraph will not be computed by the system.

For OSS packages:
When it happens and if the package version is in the OSS namespace, the
package version will not be scanned anymore. When it happens, the scan of
the package version is marked as failed and endorctl will log an error.

It should be noted that this state can not happen for tenant packages, we
always expect that tenant packages will be built for us.
 - STATUS_ERROR_PACKAGE_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE: PACKAGE_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE indicates that the package version is not
available from the package manager. This status error is only used for
unresolved dependencies.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The callgraph will not be computed by the system.

For OSS packages::
When it happens and if the package version is in the OSS namespace, the
package version will not be scanned anymore. When it happens, the scan of
the package version is marked as failed and endorctl will log an error.

It should be noted that this state can not happen for tenant packages,
for tenant we scan based on the source code and we never download a
package from a package manager.
 - STATUS_ERROR_NO_CODE_ARTIFACT: NO_CODE_ARTIFACT indicates that package version do not have any source
code. The status error is only used for call graphs.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The call graph will not be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will not be marked as a
call graph failure, only a warning log will be emitted by the system.

For OSS packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will not be marked as a
call graph failure, only a warning log will be emitted by the system.
 - STATUS_ERROR_VENV: STATUS_ERROR_VENV indicates that the system failed to create the virtual
environment required to generate the call graph.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The call graph will not be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will be not be marked as
a call graph failure. This indicates that the client code was not setup
correctly.

For OSS packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will not be marked as a
call graph failure, only a warning log will be emitted by the system.
 - STATUS_ERROR_INTERNAL: STATUS_ERROR_INTERNAL indicates that there was an internal system failure
such as a data stream error.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will be computed by the system.
- The call graph will not be computed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will be not be marked as
a call graph failure.

For OSS packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version will not be marked as a
call graph failure, only a warning log will be emitted by the system.
 - STATUS_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED: STATUS_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED indicates that we scanned a package version
having an unsupported language.

When it happens, the state of the package version will be as follows:
- The unresolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The resolved dependencies will not be computed by the system.
- The call graph will not not becomputed by the system.

For tenant packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version is marked as
unsupported.

For OSS packages:
When it happens, the scan of the package version is marked as
unsupported.

all_reachability_counts.description:
Reachability breakdown of ALL candidate-base findings (every finding
type). Populated only when Response.reachability_available is true.

vuln_reachability_counts.description:
Reachability breakdown of candidate-base VULNERABILITY findings only.
Populated only when Response.reachability_available is true.

all_counts.description: Severity counts of ALL candidate-base findings (every finding type).

all_reachability_changes.description:
all_reachability_counts minus Response.all_reachability_counts.
Negative values indicate fewer findings after the update (an
improvement). Populated only when Response.reachability_available is
true and this option is STATUS_READY.

vuln_reachability_changes.description:
vuln_reachability_counts minus Response.vuln_reachability_counts.
Populated only when Response.reachability_available is true and this
option is STATUS_READY.

all_changes.description:
all_counts minus Response.all_counts. Negative values indicate fewer
findings after the update. Unset when the candidate has not been
scanned yet (this option is STATUS_PENDING).

vuln_changes.description:
vuln_counts minus Response.vuln_counts. Unset when the candidate has
not been scanned yet (this option is STATUS_PENDING).

severity_records.description:
Top changed findings (of request.record_scope) grouped by severity (the
severity view). Each bucket holds separate fixed and introduced lists,
each ranked within the bucket and capped at
request.max_top_records_per_bucket (default 10), plus per-list totals.
Those totals reconcile with vuln_counts/vuln_changes when record_scope
is VULNERABILITY and with all_counts/all_changes when it is ALL. The
full per-bucket list is served by
ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQueryService.

reachability_records.description:
Top changed findings (of request.record_scope) grouped by reachability
(the reachability view). Same per-bucket fixed/introduced split,
capping, and totals as severity_records. Populated only when
Response.reachability_available is true.

 - STATUS_READY: The candidate base was resolved and its impact was computed.
 - STATUS_PENDING: The update option exists but its candidate PackageVersion has not
been scanned yet, so its counts and records are not yet available.

does not support reasoning.

 - AVAILABLE_LLM_GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_1_FLASH_LITE: GA Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite; in the EU it is served from the eu.rep data-residency endpoint.
 - AVAILABLE_LLM_GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5_FLASH_LITE: Generally available Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite model on Vertex AI: the
high-throughput tier of the 3.5 generation.
 - AVAILABLE_LLM_GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5_FLASH: Generally available Gemini 3.5 Flash model on Vertex AI.
 - AVAILABLE_LLM_GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_6_FLASH: Generally available Gemini 3.6 Flash model on Vertex AI: the successor to

SpecEndorLicenseBundleType.description:
Enum representing different types of Endor Labs license bundles.

 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Default value. Should not be used.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_OSS_CORE: Open Source Software (OSS) Core license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_OSS_PRO: Open Source Software (OSS) Pro license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_CICD: Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_SECRETS: Secrets Management license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_SBOM_HUB: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) Hub license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_SUPPLY_CHAIN: Supply Chain Security license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_ENDOR_PATCHING: Endor Patching license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_CODE: Discover risks in 1st party code.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_ENDOR_OUTPOST: Endor Outpost license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_SECURITY_REVIEW: Security Review license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_CODE_PRO: Discover risks in 1st party code using AI.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_OSS_FIREWALL: Endor OSS Firewall license bundle.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_BUNDLE_TYPE_AI_GOVERNANCE: AI Governance license bundle. Grants access to AI agent hook event
collection and review (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.).

SpecEndorLicenseFeatureType.description:
- ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Type is undefined.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_SCM_POSTURE_MANAGEMENT: SCM Posture Management corresponds to endorctl's Github Scanner and
ensure your respository's configuration is correct.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_SCA: SCA corresponds to endorctl's Git Scanner and runs the Software
Composition Analysis.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_SECRETS: Secrets corresponds to endorctl's Secrets Scanner.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_SBOM_INGESTION: SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) Ingestion feature for ingesting SBOM
data.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_CONTAINER_SCAN: Container Scan feature for scanning container images.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_RECOMMENDATION: Recommendation feature provides recommendations based on change impact
analysis results.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_CICD_DISCOVERY: CI/CD Discovery feature discovers CI/CD pipelines tools and
configurations.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_ARTIFACT_SIGN: Artifact Signing feature allows signing artifacts.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_ENDOR_PATCHING: Endor Patching feature allows accessing Endor Labs factory.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_SAST: SAST feature allows scanning source code for security vulnerabilities.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_AI_MODELS: AI Models feature allows scanning source code for AI model usage.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_ENDOR_OUTPOST: Endor Outpost feature allows automated scanning on-premises.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_AI_INFERENCE: AI Inference feature allows querying AI models.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_SECURITY_REVIEW: Security Review feature allows reviewing security code.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_GITHUB_ACTIONS: Github Actions feature allows scanning Github Actions workflows.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_AI_SAST: AI SAST feature allows triage/detection of false positives of SAST findings using AI.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_PACKAGE_FIREWALL: Package Firewall feature allows evaluating packages for security.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_ENDOR_ENRICHMENT: Endor Enrichment feature allows access to Endor-proprietary data.
 - ENDOR_LICENSE_FEATURE_TYPE_AI_GOVERNANCE: AI Governance feature allows recording and reviewing AI agent hook
events (e.g. Cursor, Claude Code) for governance and audit.

 - JOB_STATE_RUNNING: The job is running.
 - JOB_STATE_SUCCESS: The job has been successfully executed.
 - JOB_STATE_FAILED: The job has failed and will not be retried.
 - JOB_STATE_CANCELLED: The job has been cancelled/aborted by the service and will be retried.
 - JOB_STATE_RETRY: The job has failed but will be retried up to the max_retries limit.

SpecJobType.description:
JobType is used to match the job to its handler.
A new job type should be added when a new handler is added.

 - JOB_TYPE_SAMPLE: Sample job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_ANALYTICS_REPORT: Analytics report job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_LICENSE_REPORT: License report job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_FINDINGS_REPORT: Findings report job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_DEPENDENCIES_REPORT: Dependencies report job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_SKILL_SCORING: Skill scoring job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_CONTRIBUTOR_EXTRACTION: Contributor extraction job type. The handler iterates all projects
under the org/workspace/group identified by the job request and
extracts contributor information per project.
 - JOB_TYPE_MCP_SCORING: MCP server scoring job type. Runs the riskevaluator pipeline
against an MCP server inventory record and writes the evaluation
to McpMeta.
 - JOB_TYPE_SBOM_EXPORT: SBOM export job type. Generates a CycloneDx or SPDX SBOM for a
project or set of package versions.
 - JOB_TYPE_OBJECT_CLEANER: Object cleaner job type.
 - JOB_TYPE_VEX_EXPORT: VEX export job type. Generates a CycloneDx VEX (Vulnerability
Exploitability eXchange) document for a project or set of package
versions.
 - JOB_TYPE_AGENT_HOOK_EVENT_EXPORT: Agent hook event export job type. Streams AgentHookEvent telemetry
matching a time-bounded filter to a CSV file in object storage.

SpecUserKind.description:
UserKind says which kind of identifier the user field carries. Agents
name their users differently, so the value alone cannot be classified:
a bare login is indistinguishable from an OS login of the same spelling.
A consumer that joins identities must read this before treating a user
as an account.

 - USER_KIND_UNSPECIFIED: No kind was reported, which is what events from builds older than this
field look like. Treat the user field as unclassified rather than as
any particular kind.
 - USER_KIND_EMAIL: Account email the agent itself reports.
 - USER_KIND_GITHUB_LOGIN: GitHub account handle, which is all GitHub Copilot records locally.
 - USER_KIND_OS_LOGIN: No agent account was resolved, so the user field repeats os_user.
Never join on this as an account: one shared machine would merge every
developer who used it into a single identity.
 - USER_KIND_ASSERTED: Identifier supplied by the operator through the environment rather than
read from the agent, so its shape is whatever the fleet configured.

VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQueryServic.description:
VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQuery patches the metadata of stored documents
without touching their content or embeddings.

Re-uploading a document cannot do this: the upload path skips any document
whose uniqueness key and content hash already match what is stored, so a
metadata-only change is silently dropped. Deleting and re-adding would work
but re-embeds every document and leaves a window where the document is
missing, which for summary stores means an interrupted run re-pays the LLM
that produced it. This applies the patch in place instead.

clientBucket.description:
A Bucket of a conventional histogram, each of which is treated as
an individual counter-like time series by Prometheus.

offset.description: Gap to previous span, or starting point for 1st span (which can be negative).

clientBucketSpan.description:
A BucketSpan defines a number of consecutive buckets in a native
histogram with their offset. Logically, it would be more
straightforward to include the bucket counts in the Span. However,
the protobuf representation is more compact in the way the data is
structured here (with all the buckets in a single array separate
from the Spans).

bucket.description:
Buckets for the conventional histogram.

Ordered in increasing order of upper_bound, +Inf bucket is optional.

schema.description:
schema defines the bucket schema. Currently, valid numbers are -4 <= n <= 8.
They are all for base-2 bucket schemas, where 1 is a bucket boundary in each case, and
then each power of two is divided into 2^n logarithmic buckets.
Or in other words, each bucket boundary is the previous boundary times 2^(2^-n).
In the future, more bucket schemas may be added using numbers < -4 or > 8.

negative_span.description: Negative buckets for the native histogram.

negative_delta.description:
Use either "negative_delta" or "negative_count", the former for
regular histograms with integer counts, the latter for float
histograms.

Count delta of each bucket compared to previous one (or to zero for 1st bucket).

positive_span.description:
Positive buckets for the native histogram.
Use a no-op span (offset 0, length 0) for a native histogram without any
observations yet and with a zero_threshold of 0. Otherwise, it would be
indistinguishable from a classic histogram.

positive_delta.description:
Use either "positive_delta" or "positive_count", the former for
regular histograms with integer counts, the latter for float
histograms.

Count delta of each bucket compared to previous one (or to zero for 1st bucket).

exemplars.description: Only used for native histograms. These exemplars MUST have a timestamp.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

googlerpcStatus.description:

different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is
used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains
three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.

You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the
[API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

v1AISASTScanCache.description:
AISASTScanCache tracks scan outcomes at file-level granularity for AI SAST
incremental scanning. Each document contains the segments for a single
file, enabling efficient bulk reads and writes against MongoDB. When the
outcome changes (e.g. a previously failed file is retried successfully),
the existing cache entry is updated in place.

This is a cache: LinterResults remain the authoritative finding records.
If the cache is lost, the system falls back to a full scan.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project this scan cache entry belongs to.

file_path.description: Relative file path within the repository (e.g. "src/api/handler.go").

content_hash.description:
SHA-256 hex hash of the full file content. Uses the same hashing
approach as repoindexer/indexer.go calculateHash.

outcome.description: The scan outcome shared by all segments in this document.

scanned_at_sha.description: The commit SHA at which these segments were last scanned.

scanned_at.description: Timestamp of the last scan attempt for this file.

ref.description:
Git ref whose scan wrote this entry, as it appears on the scanned
RepositoryVersion (e.g. "main", "refs/heads/release/1.2").

Attribution only, never a key. Entries are keyed by content hash so that
refs sharing a file's content share its entry, which is what keeps the
cost of scanning a second ref close to zero. A shared entry therefore
names whichever ref wrote it last: read this to understand where an entry
came from, and do not branch behavior on it.

source_repository_version_uuid.description:
RepositoryVersion whose LinterResults hold the findings these segments
produced. Set to the scanned version, which is not necessarily the
version this entry is parented to.

A cache hit means "this content was already scanned"; it does not mean the
findings are attached to the version being scanned now. This field names
where they are, so a hit can be turned back into findings for another ref.

Left unset rather than empty when the scanning version is unknown, so the
pattern requires a real UUID whenever the field is present.

agent_id.description:
The join key to the agent catalog (EndorAgent.id), recorded verbatim from
the token's agent_id claim. It is never derived by splitting agent_identity
(id@version), so it stays stable against the catalog. An id with no catalog
entry is still returned, not dropped.

agent_identity.description:
The {name}@{version} identity from the agent's JWT (agent_identity claim).
Unset for an unregistered agent, distinct from a recorded empty identity.

calls.description: Total captured backend calls in the window.

allowed.description: Calls the authorization + mutability gates allowed.

denied.description: Calls denied (e.g. a read-only agent attempting a mutation).

sessions.description:
Distinct agent-run sessions in the window, as an approximate upper bound:
per-day distinct counts are summed, so a session spanning midnight counts in
each day it touches. Reconciliation populates it; the incremental capture path
does not. Unset whenever the summed count is zero — not yet reconciled or none
recorded — so a consumer renders it as absent rather than a definite 0.

last_seen.description: When the agent was last seen making a call. Unset if it never has.

active.description:
True if the agent made at least one call in the window. Always true for an
entry in this response, which lists only agents with in-window activity.

v1AgentActivity.description:
AgentActivity is the per-agent usage summary for one agent. Keyed by
agent_id, the join key to the agent catalog (EndorAgent.id).

timestamp.description: When the edge observed the call.

operation.description:

Unset when the operation could not be derived, distinct from a recorded
empty verb.

resource_kind.description: The Endor resource the call operated on (e.g. Project).

rpc_method.description: Full gRPC method, for engineers who want the exact RPC.

status_code.description: gRPC status code name (e.g. OK, PermissionDenied).

session.description: The agent-run session this call belongs to; unset for a call with no session.

on_behalf_of.description: The human principal the agent acted on behalf of; unset when none.

scopes.description:
The scope the call ran under, e.g. customer-full; comma-joined when more than
one. Unset when none were recorded.
