v1AgentConfig.description: Represents the information captured from an AgentConfig of endorctl.

mcp_servers.description: McpServers lists the MCP servers configured at this level.

sandbox.description: Sandbox holds sandbox network and filesystem rules.

permissions.description: Permissions holds tool and command permission rules.

hooks.description: Hooks lists the hook event bindings configured at this level.

env.description: Env holds environment variables configured at this level.

instruction_files.description:
InstructionFiles lists rule/instruction files discovered at this level.
Cursor: .mdc files from rules/ directories. Claude Code: reserved for future use.

default_model.description:
DefaultModel is the default model ID configured at this level.
Populated from Claude Code settings only.

available_models.description:
AvailableModels restricts which model IDs are selectable.
Populated from Claude Code settings only.

environment_type.description:
EnvironmentType is the remote environment type (e.g. "docker").
Populated from Cursor environment.json only.

v1AgentConfigLevel.description:
AgentConfigLevel captures the agent configuration at one scope level
(repository, user, or enterprise).

repository.description: Repository holds config from the workspace's .claude/ or .cursor/ directory.

user.description: User holds config from the user's home directory (~/.claude/ or ~/.cursor/).

enterprise.description: Enterprise holds config from the OS-managed enterprise config path.

v1AgentConfigSnapshot.description:
AgentConfigSnapshot captures the three-level configuration hierarchy
(repository, user, enterprise) at session start time.

system_prompt.description: SystemPrompt is the system prompt that the agent will use.

tool_names.description:
tool_names is the list of tool names that the agent will use.
It must be one of the supported tools. If the tool is not supported, the
request will fail.

llm.description:
LLM is the LLM that the agent will use. It must be one of the supported
LLMs.

options.description: Options is the options that the agent will use.

vector_store_uuid.description: VectorStoreUUID is the vector store that the agent can use.

local_execution_only.description: LocalExecutionOnly is true if the agent can only be executed locally.

feedback.description: Show feedback to the user (e.g. "are you sure you want to do this?").

alert.description: Raise an alert (e.g. "user should not be messing with this file").

ask.description: Ask the user with a message (e.g. "are you sure you want to do this?").

v1AgentHookAction.description: Action describes how to match the activity with the policy and what to do when it matches.

mcp_tool_call.description: Match MCP tool calls (server + tool + optional input matchers).

file_access.description: Match file access by operation and path patterns.

skill.description: Match skills by name and/or score thresholds.

mcp_server.description:
Match MCP servers by name and/or score thresholds (server-level,
not tool-call-level).

session.description:
Match sessions by posture predicates over SessionHook fields and
the captured AgentConfigSnapshot.

malware_check.description: Check the packages in an install command against Endor's malware feed.

secrets_check.description: Scan file content (write/edit proposed content, or a read) for secrets.

v1AgentHookActivity.description: Activity describes what kind of hook activity the policy applies to.

event_name.description: EventName is the lifecycle hook event name (e.g. "PostToolUse").

commands.description: Commands lists the shell commands registered for this event.

v1AgentHookConfig.description:
AgentHookConfig represents one hook event binding: the event that triggers
it and the commands that run in response.

uuid.description: The UUID of an AgentHookEvent.

tenant_meta.description: AgentHookEvent are associated with a tenant or are global.

spec.description: The internal specification of the object.

processing_result.description: Result of downstream processing (inventory, dashboard, etc.).

consumers_failed.description: Consumer keys that failed to process this event. Used for retry.

v1AgentHookEvent.description:
AgentHookEvent represents a single event emitted by the agent runtime.
Each event has a type, context, and optional type-specific payload.

session_id.description: Session identifier for the agent run.

sub_session_id.description: Sub-session identifier for the agent run.

cwd.description: Working directory when the event was captured.

raw_hook_event_name.description: Raw hook event name from the agent.

error_message.description: Error message if the hook event failed.

is_interrupted.description: Whether the hook event was interrupted.

has_policy_violation.description: Set to true when policy_matches is non-empty.

identity.description:
Org identity resolved for this session against the org directory.
Populated at SessionStart and attached to every event in the session
so policy can match on role / group. Absent when the directory
resolve did not succeed.

os_user.description:
Operating-system login of the account running the agent, carried
alongside user rather than instead of it, and populated even when it
repeats user.

This is the key that links one person's agent accounts, because the same
developer is an email to one agent and a GitHub handle to another while
staying one OS login underneath. Pair it with device_id: on a shared
machine or a CI runner the login is a generic name such as "runner" or
"root", and joining on it alone merges unrelated people.

user_kind.description: Which kind of identifier the user field carries.

action.description: Action to take when the activity matches.

name.description: Name of the policy.

system.description: Whether this is a system-defined policy (vs user-defined).

inventory_classification.description:
Inventory classification this policy assigns to a matched MCP server
or skill. Projected onto AgenticInventory by the aiapiserver inventory
consumers. Unset / UNSPECIFIED means the policy does not affect
inventory classification.

scope.description:
Cross-cutting scope restricting which events this policy applies to,
independent of activity kind. Unset means the policy applies to every
event (back-compatible default).

v1AgentHookPolicy.description:
AgentHookPolicy describes a policy to apply when agent hook events match a
given activity. When the activity matches, the action (e.g. feedback, block,
alert) is applied.

uuid.description: The UUID of an AgentHookPolicyDefinition.

tenant_meta.description: AgentHookPolicyDefinitions are associated with a tenant or are global.

spec.description: The internal specification of the object.

propagate.description:
Object can be propagated to child namespaces. Global objects are visible to
all namespaces.

v1AgentHookPolicyDefinition.description:
AgentHookPolicyDefinition is a top-level CRUD object that stores a single
AgentHookPolicy alongside standard metadata.

policy.description: The policy stored in this definition.

session.description: Session match (posture predicates over SessionHook + AgentConfigSnapshot).

malware.description: Malware match (a package flagged by the malware check on an install).

secrets.description: Secrets match (a secret detected in file content by the secrets check).

repository_matchers.description:
Regex matchers for the repository from AgentHookEvent.Spec.repository
(e.g. "github\\.com/acme/.*", ".*-infra$"). OR'd among themselves.

user_matchers.description:
Regex matchers for the user/account from AgentHookEvent.Spec.user
(e.g. "alice", "svc-.*", ".*@example\\.com"). "Account" in the ticket
maps to this per-session user identity; there is no separate account
entity. OR'd among themselves.

v1AgentHookPolicyScope.description:
AgentHookPolicyScope restricts a policy to a subset of events by matching
against per-event identity carried on AgentHookEvent.Spec (repository, user).
Scope is evaluated once, before activity-kind matching, so it applies
uniformly to all activity kinds.

Match logic: an unset scope (or a scope with no matchers set) applies to
every event. When set, configured matcher branches are AND'd — every set
branch must produce a hit; within a branch the regexes are OR'd (any one
matching satisfies the branch); an empty branch is ignored. A scope miss
makes the policy a no-op for the event for both blocklist and allowlist
match types (the policy simply does not apply).

email.description: Corporate email of the resolved user.

display_name.description: Display name of the resolved user.

groups.description: Org groups / teams the user belongs to.

v1AgentIdentity.description:
AgentIdentity is the org identity resolved for the account behind an event,
sourced from the agent provider's org directory. Only the caller's own
identity is ever resolved on a client (self-scoped).

name.description: Name is the base filename without extension (e.g. "security" from "security.mdc").

path.description: Path is the absolute filesystem path to the instruction file.

content_hash.description: ContentHash is the SHA-256 hex digest of the file content.

v1AgentInstructionFile.description:
AgentInstructionFile represents a rule or instruction file discovered during
configuration scanning. Content is not stored; only paths and hashes are
captured to detect changes without exposing potentially sensitive content.

name.description:
Name is the canonical runtime identifier of the MCP server program — the
value extracted from the command line (e.g. "endorctl" from
"npx -y endorctl ai-tools mcp-server") or, for HTTP/SSE servers, the host
slice of the URL. The backend uses this as the inventory document name
so SESSION_START rows and per-tool rows (whose McpToolHook.server_name
is derived the same way from the runtime URL/command) land on a single
inventory document per logical server.

command.description: Command is the executable used for stdio-transport servers.

args.description: Args are the command-line arguments passed to the server process.

env.description: Env holds environment variables injected into the server process.

url.description: URL is the endpoint for HTTP or SSE transport servers.

transport.description:
Transport is the MCP transport type: "stdio", "http", or "sse".
Collectors must populate this; an empty value means the collector could
not classify the server. Claude Code reads this from .mcp.json; Cursor
derives it structurally from command/url since mcp.json has no transport
field.

headers.description:
Headers are additional HTTP headers sent with requests.
Populated by collectors when available; Cursor's mcp.json has no headers
field so this is empty for Cursor.

config_server_name.description:
ConfigServerName is the user-authored mcp.json map key that named this
server entry in the agent's configuration (e.g. "claude-endor-cli-tools",
"postgres"). It is the stable identifier per-tool hooks can use to look
the entry up in the cached SESSION_START snapshot — Claude's tool name
shape "mcp__<server>__<tool>" carries this value, while Name carries the
runtime program identity. Wrapped to distinguish "unset" from "".

v1AgentMCPServer.description: AgentMCPServer represents a single named MCP server entry common to all agents.

allowed_tools.description:
AllowedTools lists MCP tool names that are auto-approved.
Populated primarily from Cursor configs; Claude Code uses rule strings instead.

denied_tools.description: DeniedTools lists MCP tool names that are blocked.

allowed_commands.description:
AllowedCommands lists shell command patterns that are auto-approved.
For Claude Code these are permission rule strings (e.g. "Bash(git:*)").

denied_commands.description: DeniedCommands lists shell command patterns that are blocked.

allowed_mcp_servers.description:
AllowedMcpServers lists MCP server names permitted by managed policy.
Populated from Claude Code managed settings; empty for Cursor.

denied_mcp_servers.description:
DeniedMcpServers lists MCP server names blocked by managed policy.
Populated from Claude Code managed settings; empty for Cursor.

additional_directories.description:
AdditionalDirectories lists extra working directories the agent may access.
Claude Code: from permissions.additionalDirectories. Cursor: from CLI allowedPaths.

default_mode.description:
DefaultMode is the permission mode used when no explicit rule matches.
Populated from Claude Code only (e.g. "default", "bypassPermissions").

bypass_disabled.description:
BypassDisabled indicates whether bypass-permissions mode is disabled.
Populated from Claude Code only.

v1AgentPermissionsConfig.description: AgentPermissionsConfig normalizes permission rules across agents.

allowed_network_hosts.description: AllowedNetworkHosts lists hostnames/domains the agent may reach.

blocked_network_hosts.description:
BlockedNetworkHosts lists hostnames/domains the agent may not reach.
Populated from Cursor configs only; Claude Code uses allowlist-only.

writable_paths.description: WritablePaths lists filesystem paths the agent may write to.

readable_paths.description: ReadablePaths lists filesystem paths the agent may read from.

enabled.description:
Enabled indicates whether sandboxing is turned on.
Wrapped to distinguish "unset" from "false".

fail_if_unavailable.description:
FailIfUnavailable causes the agent to exit when sandboxing is unavailable.
Wrapped to distinguish "unset" from "false".

v1AgentSandboxConfig.description: AgentSandboxConfig normalizes sandbox network and filesystem rules across agents.

uuid.description:
The uuid of the resource. This is also the session ID for a user
that wants to continue a conversation with the agent.
It will accumulate messages over the conversation.

tenant_meta.description: The tenant metadata restricts access to a specific tenant.

v1AgentSession.description: Implements an agent session by interacting with the implemented agents.

uuid.description: The UUID of the query.

tenant_meta.description: Agent session count queries are associated with a tenant.

v1AgentSessionCountQuery.description:
AgentSessionCountQuery is an internal API returning the total number of
agent sessions in a namespace. Unlike ListAgentSessions, results are not
restricted to sessions owned by or shared with the caller: the response
carries only a count, so no session content can be exposed.

time_range.description:
Optional time range filter on session creation time.
When unset, all sessions in the namespace are counted.

traverse.description: Whether to include child namespaces in the count.

count.description: Total number of agent sessions matching the request.

agent_contexts.description:
agent_contexts can include multiple instances of AgentContext. The context
can only be provided at the beginning of a session and cannot be updated
later on.

message_history.description: The previous messages in the session.

request.description: The current message request in the session.

owner_claims.title: owner claims representing the owner of the session (ie user)

shared_session.description:
shared_session indicates if this session is shared with other users.
If true, the session will be visible to all users in the same namespace.

uuid.description: The uuid of the resource.

tenant_meta.description: The tenant metadata restricts access to a specific tenant.

v1AgentTool.description: Lists the available Agent Tools that can be attached to agents.

uuid.description: The UUID of an AgentWorkflow.

tenant_meta.description: AgentWorkflows are associated with a tenant or are global.

spec.description: The internal specification of the object.

propagate.description:
Object can be propagated to child namespaces. Global objects are visible to
all namespaces.

v1AgentWorkflow.description:
Represents an agent workflow that orchestrates multiple agents.
Workflows can be of different types, such as chain, planner, or swarm.
The initial implementation supports chain workflows where agents execute
sequentially, passing outputs to the next agent in the chain.

uuid.description: The UUID of the aggregate record.

tenant_meta.description: Aggregate is associated with a tenant.

spec.description: The internal specification of the aggregate.

v1AgenticAggregate.description:
AgenticAggregate stores time-bucketed aggregated metrics from AgentHookEvents.
One document per (namespace, aggregate_bucket, bucket_granularity, dimension_key, dimension_value).

aggregate_bucket.description: Time bucket (UTC, truncated to the granularity).

dimension_key.description: Aggregation dimension (e.g. by agent, model, command).

dimension_value.description: Value within the dimension (e.g. agent name, model name, command binary).

bucket_granularity.description: Time granularity of the aggregate bucket (e.g. hourly, daily).

sessions.description: Total number of session events within the aggregate bucket.

tool_calls.description: Number of tool invocations (e.g. agent tool calls).

executions.description: Total number of command executions within this bucket.

read_operations.description: Number of read-type operations (e.g. file reads, data retrieval).

write_operations.description: Number of write-type operations (e.g. file writes, data modification).

file_access_events.description: Number of events where files were accessed (read, write, edit, etc).

user_prompts.description: Total number of user prompts or messages handled.

errors.description: Number of error events encountered in this bucket.

interrupted.description: Number of events where operations were interrupted or cancelled.

edit_operations.description: Number of file or entity edit operations.

delete_operations.description: Number of delete operations (e.g. files, records).

users.description: Number of distinct users who generated events in this bucket.

repositories.description: Number of distinct repositories seen in events for this bucket.

uuid.description: The UUID of the inventory record.

tenant_meta.description: Inventory is associated with a tenant.

spec.description: The internal specification of the inventory.

v1AgenticInventory.description:
AgenticInventory represents aggregated metrics for agents, models, MCP servers, skills, and AI tools.
One collection with type discriminator. Upserted on agent hook events.

type.description: Type discriminator for the unified inventory collection.

name.description: Unique name within the type (e.g. server name for MCP, agent name, model name).

error_hook_events.description: Number of hook events that had an error.

total_duration_msec.description: Sum of all hook event durations in milliseconds.

last_seen.description: Timestamp when this inventory was last seen (most recent activity).

active_sessions.description:
Number of sessions currently in progress (incremented on SESSION_START,
decremented on SESSION_STOP).

interrupted_hook_events.description: Number of events that were interrupted.

users.description: Number of distinct users that triggered events for this inventory item.

repositories.description: Number of distinct repositories associated with this inventory item.

v1AiToolCategory.description: AiToolCategory classifies a detected AI development tool.

v1AiToolDetection.description: AiToolDetection represents a single detected AI development tool.

v1AiToolEvidence.description: AiToolEvidence is a single key-value signal supporting an AI tool detection.

v1AiToolInventory.description: AiToolInventory contains all AI development tools detected on the host machine.

feedback_message.description: Feedback message shown to the user when the alert is raised.

v1AlertAction.description: AlertAction records an alert with a message (e.g. for audit).

description.description: Short human readable description of the allowlist.

regexes.description: A slice of content regular expressions that are allowed to be ignored.

paths.description: A slice of path regular expressions that are allowed to be ignored.

commits.description: A slice of commit SHAs that are allowed to be ignored.

stop_words.description:
A slice of stop words that are allowed to be ignored.
This targets the _secret_, not the content of the regex match like the
regexes slice.

condition.description:
Match condition for this allowlist ("OR" or "AND"). Defaults to "OR".
When "AND", all criteria must match for the allowlist to apply.

v1Allowlist.description: Allows a rule to be ignored for specific regexes, paths, and/or commits.

uuid.description: The UUID of a AnalyticsExecutionRecord resource.

tenant_meta.description: Analytic records are associated with a tenant.

v1AnalyticsExecutionRecord.description: Captures the status, time and stats of an execution of the analytics.

platform_source.description: The platform to which the parent repository belongs.

analytics_time.description:
Represents the last time a repository was analysed.

Timestamp is represented in the RFC 3339 format, for example, 2017-01-15T01:30:15.01Z.

RFC 3339: https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.txt

analytics_state.description: The status of the analytics run.

execution_stats.description: The execution stats generated during the analysis.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project to which the execution record belongs.

username.description:
The username (or Atlassian account email for Scoped API Tokens) used for
HTTP Basic Auth against Bitbucket Cloud.

app_password.description:
The App Password or Atlassian Scoped API Token used for HTTP Basic Auth.
Both credential types are wire-compatible (username:token in Basic Auth header).

v1AppPasswordConfig.description:
AppPasswordConfig holds HTTP Basic Auth credentials for Bitbucket Cloud.
It supports both legacy App Passwords and its replacement, Atlassian
Scoped API Tokens (https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/api-tokens/).
Both use the same HTTP Basic Auth mechanism (username:token).
NOTE: Bitbucket App Passwords are deprecated and will be removed on June 9, 2026.
New integrations should use Scoped API Tokens.

v1ApproveServiceRequest.description: ApproveServiceRequest defines a message for approving or denying service requests.

service_request_uuid.description: The service request for which the approval request is associated.

comment.description: The reasoning behind the decision by the approver.

status.description: The approval or denial decision by the approver for the given request.

name.description: Full name of the artifact with extension type.

checksum.description: Checksum of the artifact, used to verify data integrity.

v1ArtifactDownloadType.description: ArtifactDownloadType identifies the kind of artifact downloaded for malware detection.

tenant_meta.description: The tenant metadata restrict access to a specific tenant.

response.description: Response contains the result of the executed artifacts command.

v1ArtifactOperation.description: ArtifactOperation implements the artifacts operations on the server side.

v1ArtifactOperationCommand.description:
- ARTIFACT_OPERATION_COMMAND_SIGN: ARTIFACT_OPERATION_COMMAND_SIGN is used to sign an artifact.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_COMMAND_VERIFY: ARTIFACT_OPERATION_COMMAND_VERIFY is used to verify an artifact.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_COMMAND_REVOKE_SIGNATURE: ARTIFACT_OPERATION_COMMAND_REVOKE_SIGNATURE is used to revoke an artifact signature.

result.description: The result of the artifact operation.

artifact_signature.description:
In case of successful verification, this holds information about
the signature event, which includes the signature, the time of the signing event
as well as the various attestations.

v1ArtifactOperationResult.description:
The result of an artifact operation.

 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_UNSPECIFIED: No validator.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_SUCCESS: Success in the artifact operation.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_NO_ARTIFACT: Couldn't find any signatures for the given artifact name.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_NO_SIGNATURE: No signature found for the given digest of the artifact.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_TIME_MISMATCH: The timestamp associated with the signature is outside the
time window of the validity of the certificate.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_INVALID_SIGNATURE: The stored signature is invalid.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_UNKNOWN_CA: Unable to verify with a known CA.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_REVOKED_SIGNATURE: Signature has been revoked.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_CLAIMS_MISMATCH: Claims/attestations in the signature don't match input.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_BAD_CERTIFICATE: Empty or corrupted certificate.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_INVALID_KEY_TYPE: Could not find the right type of key in the certificate.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_CORRUPTED_SIGNATURE: Could not decode signature.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_KEY_GEN_FAILURE: Failed to generate private key.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_CSR_GEN_FAILURE: Failed to generate certificate request.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_SIGN_FAILURE: Failed to sign.
 - ARTIFACT_OPERATION_RESULT_INVALID_ARTIFACT_NAME: Invalid artifact name.

artifact_name.description: The name of the artifact being signed or verified.

digest.description:
Used only for the REVOKE command and is the source repository digest for the
signature to be revoked. The artifact name has to be provided as well.

extensions.description: Certificate extensions for artifact signing operations.

artifact_type.description: The type of the artifact being signed or verified.

uuid.description: The UUID of an artifact signature object.

meta.description: Metadata is generic for any object.

tenant_meta.description: Tenant metadata required for artifact signature requests.

certificate.description: The certificate obtained for this sign operation.

signature.description: The signature of the build artifact.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the signing event.

revoked.description: Set to true if the signature gets revoked.

artifact_type.description: The type of artifact for this signature.

source_repository_ref.description:
Source repository ref. This also exists in the certificate but it's also here
to quickly look up entries that match.

provenance.description: Provenance information for this build artifact.

feedback_message.description: Feedback message shown to the user when asking for confirmation.

v1AskAction.description: AskAction allows asking the user with a message.

uuid.description: The UUID of the assured package version.

tenant_meta.description: Git repositories are associated with a tenant.

meta.description: Metadata are generic for any object.

v1AssuredPackageVersion.description:
AssuredPackageVersion is a  package version that have been built, tested, and patched by Endor Labs.
It includes details on how the version was built, tested, and patched, as well as information on the vulnerabilities that have been addressed through the patches.

package_name.description:
The name of the package of this assured package version. It is
calculated automatically from the assured package version name.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the assured package version.
For Java, this is the SHA of the jar file.

reproducible_build_source_code_url.description:
The URL to download the source code
to reproduce the build of the package version.
This is a signed URL valid only for four hours.

upgrade_summary.description: Contains the upgrade summary with the package version.

uuid.description:
UUID of the AsyncJob. Assigned by the server on Create; use it to
fetch the job via GetAsyncJob.

tenant_meta.description: Tenant the async job belongs to.

v1AsyncJob.description:
AsyncJob is an asynchronous job — SBOM export or VEX export
types today, with more types added as they ship.

type.description: The kind of async job to run.

v1AsyncJobSpecRequest.description: Wrapper holding the type-specific request arm.

error_message.description: Reason for failure. Populated when state = Job.Spec.JobState.JOB_STATE_FAILED.

v1AsyncJobSpecResponse.description: Wrapper holding the type-specific response arm and any error message.

v1AsyncJobType.description:
The kind of async job being run.

 - TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unset.
 - TYPE_SBOM: Software Bill of Materials.
 - TYPE_VEX: Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange.

message_uuid.description: Represents the UUID of the resource which is accessed.

authorized_tenants.description: The tenants accessible by this user at the time of authentication.

error_message.description: Error message details if the authentication fails.

Claims in the context.

v1AuthenticationResponse.description: Response to the request includes a token and the token expiration time for an authenticated user.

uuid.description: The UUID of the authorization request.

meta.description: Metadata is generic for any object.

claims.description: Establishes the list of claims for attribute based access control.

target_namespace.description:
The target namespace of the request. If empty, the request is for a global object
that doesn't have a namespace.

permissions.description:
The set of allowed permissions.

For the given claims, the caller has the permissions described below for every
API call. If an API call is not included, then it is not authorized.

v1Authorization.description: Represents an authorization request in the system.

uuid.description: The UUID of the AuthorizationPolicy resource.

tenant_meta.description: Authorization policies are associated with a tenant.

meta.description: Metadata is generic for any object.

propagate.description: Indicates that the object should be visible in the child namespaces.

v1AuthorizationPolicy.description: Represents an authorization policy in the system.

clause.description:
The list of claims that must match. This is essentially
an AND operator. User claims must match all the
criteria in the clause for the policy to match.

For example, ["group=X", "email=user@endor.ai"] will match
users of group X with this email.

Clause strings must contain only allowed characters to prevent XSS attacks
and ensure exact matching with incoming JWT claims. Allowed characters:
letters, numbers, and the following: =@._-/: +()& (space, plus, parentheses, ampersand).

target_namespaces.description:
The target namespaces of the policy. The policy can
apply to one or more target namespaces. The targets
can only be the current namespace or its children.

propagate.description:
Propagate indicates that the policy should include
the children of the target namespace as well as allowed targets.

expiration_time.description:
Disables this policy after its expiration time.
If expiration time is not provided, the policy will never expire.

is_support_policy.description:
is_support_policy indicates that the policy is a support policy and
cannot be altered without using the SupportAccess API.

v1AutoDetectResult.description: Message for an auto detect result.

full_pr_scan.description: full_pr_scan indicates whether a full scan should be enabled during PRs.

full_push_scan.description:
full_push_scan indicates whether a full scan should be enabled during
pushes.

included_paths.description: included_paths is a list of paths that should be included in the scan.

excluded_paths.description: excluded_paths is a list of paths that should be excluded from the scan.

languages.description:
languages is a list of languages that should be scanned. If emtpy
default values are used.

call_graph_languages.description:
call_graph_languages is the list of languages that should be used to
calculate call graphs. If empty, default values are used.

bazel_configuration.description:
bazel_configuration is the configuration that should be used for Bazel
builds. If populated, scans are performed as a bazel repository.

additional_environment_variables.description:
additional_environment_variables sets extra environment variables for the
scan, specific to languages or tools. By design only ENDOR_-prefixed
variables are honored; any entry without the ENDOR_ prefix is silently
dropped, as are a few reserved ENDOR_ variables the scanner sets itself.

enable_automated_pr_scans.description:
enable_automated_pr_scans for this repository will allow the github
app to selectively scan PRs and merges for this repository.
If the project is not part of a github app, this setting will be ingored.

disable_code_storage.description:
disable_code_storage is a boolean value that indicates if the source code related to a finding
should be stored or displayed. Default will be off.

disable_code_snippet_storage.description:
disable_code_snippet_storage is a boolean value that indicates if the source code snippet
related to a finding should be stored or displayed. Default will be off.

enable_pr_security_review_scan.description: enable_pr_security_review_scan is a boolean value that indicates if a Security Review scan should be requested.

enable_pr_incremental_scan.description: enable_pr_incremental_scan is a boolean value that indicates if the PR incremental scan should be requested.

enable_ai_sast_scan.description: enable_ai_sast_scan is a boolean value that indicates if AI SAST scan should be requested.

segment_match_languages.description:
segment_match_languages is the list of languages to enable segment-match based analysis for.
Clears the default languages if languages is not set explicitly.

v1AutomatedScanParameters.description:
AutomatedScanParameters represents the parameters that must be applied during
automated cloud scans to the projects associated with the corresponding
profile.

v1AutomatedScanParametersConfig.description: Message for automated scan parameter configuration.

personal_access_token.description: PAT of the user doing integration to fetch resources using REST APIs.

webhook_secret.description:
The shared password configured as the basic authentication credential for
Azure DevOps Service Hook deliveries belonging to this installation.

enable_pr_scans.description:
enable_pr_scans is a boolean value that indicates if automated PR scans
are enabled for Azure DevOps repositories.

enable_pr_comments.description:
enable_pr_comments is a boolean value that indicates if automated PR
comments are enabled for Azure DevOps repositories.

enable_full_scan.description:
enable_full_scan is a boolean value that indicates if the full scan should
be enabled for Azure DevOps PR scans.

pull_request_payload.description:
pull_request_payload contains the raw Azure DevOps pull request Service
Hook payload as JSON. The originating PR number lives at
"resource.pullRequestId".

v1AzurePayload.description:
AzurePayload carries SCM-specific webhook data for an Azure DevOps-originated
scan. Mirrors GitHubPayload so downstream components (e.g., AI SAST baseline
lookup) can recover the originating PR number on merge-to-main webhook events
where pull_request_id is intentionally blank.

uuid.description: The finding UUID.

target_dependency_package.description:
Fully qualified dependency package in "ecosystem://package@version" form.
Populated from the finding's spec.target_dependency_package_name when set,
otherwise from dependency_package_version_metadata.meta.name. Never the
bare target_dependency_name.

vulnerability_id.description:
Preferred single vulnerability identifier for VULNERABILITY findings: the
CVE ID when the advisory has one, otherwise the primary advisory ID (e.g. a
GHSA). Empty for non-vulnerability findings. For the complete set of IDs use
vulnerability_ids.

vulnerability_ids.description:
All identifiers for the advisory behind a VULNERABILITY finding: the primary
advisory ID (vulnerability.meta.name) first, followed by every alias
(vulnerability.spec.aliases, e.g. CVE / GHSA cross-references), de-duplicated
and order-preserving. Empty for non-vulnerability findings.

summary.description:
Human-readable finding text, copied from the finding's spec.summary
(e.g. "<pkg> has a <type> vulnerability identified by <id>: <summary>. ...").

finding_tags.description:
Projected reachability of the finding's dependency in the app image.
Populated only when Response.reachability_available is true.

v1BaseImageFindingRecord.description:
BaseImageFindingRecord is a compact projection of one changed finding in the
base-image update impact record lists (the per-bucket fixed/introduced lists
and the records drill-down page). Feature-local by design: it is intentionally
NOT the shared FindingSummaryInfo, so the version-upgrade surface that consumes
that message is left untouched.

tenant_meta.description:
Information about the tenant to which the root package (importer)
belongs.

v1BatchDependencyMetadata.description: Request to create multiple DependencyMetadata objects.

tenant_meta.description: Namespace of the file segments.

v1BatchFileSegments.description: Request used to create or delete multiple file segment objects.

tenant_meta.description: Information about the tenant.

v1BatchNotification.description: Request to create multiple Notification objects.

finding_uuids.description: List of finding UUIDs to create notifications.

uuid.description: The uuid of the resource.

tenant_meta.description: Namespace all queries in the batch belong to.

v1BatchPackageLicenseQuery.description:
BatchPackageLicenseQuery groups multiple PackageLicenseQuery requests into a single call.
The server evaluates each item and populates its output fields (licenses, copyrights,
notices, applied_overrides) before returning the object.

access_token.title:
The access token associated with the Bitbucket Cloud account.
https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/access-tokens

host_url.description: The URL of the workspace (only for cloud) or project.

webhook_secret.description:
The webhook secret configured in Bitbucket for validating incoming webhook
events.

enable_pr_scans.description:
enable_pr_scans is a boolean value that indicates if the automated PR scans
are enabled.

enable_pr_comments.description:
enable_pr_comments is a boolean value that indicates if the automated PR
comments should be enabled.

enable_full_scan.description:
enable_full_scan is a boolean value that indicates if the full scan should
be enabled.

http_access_token.description: The HTTP Access Token used for Bitbucket Datacenter authentication.

pull_request_payload.description:
pull_request_payload contains the raw Bitbucket pull request webhook
payload as JSON. The originating PR number lives at "pullrequest.id"
(Bitbucket Cloud) or "pullRequest.id" (Bitbucket Data Center).

v1BitbucketPayload.description:
BitbucketPayload carries SCM-specific webhook data for a Bitbucket-originated
scan (Bitbucket Cloud or Bitbucket Data Center). Mirrors GitHubPayload so
downstream components (e.g., AI SAST baseline lookup) can recover the
originating PR number on merge-to-main webhook events where pull_request_id
is intentionally blank.

feedback_message.description: Feedback message shown to the user when the action is blocked.

v1BlockAction.description: BlockAction blocks the activity and shows a message.

v1BlockReason.description:
BlockReason represents the reason why a package was blocked.
Deprecated: use PackageFirewallLog.Reason instead.

dependency_graph.title:
A dependency graph is a K/V pair of package names.
The format of the key must be:
- mvn://MVN_CENTRAL/foo:bar@2.1
- mvn://CLIENT_REPO/foo:bar@2.1-SNAPSHOT
- go://github.com/myorg/myrepo/mypkg@sha

dependencies.description:
Different package managers use different dependency graph serialization
strategies. Include the serialized list here to avoid re-implementing
this within endoctl.

dependency_files.description:
The list of the dependency files used to create the BOM.
This field is optional and is only set when the source code of the
package versions is known. It will contain the list of relative path of
files used to compute the BOM. For instance for Golang, it will contain
the go.mod and go.sum.

allow_create.description: Anyone with write access to the repository can create a new branch.

allow_delete.description: Anyone with write access to the repository can delete a branch.

allow_force_push.description: Anyone with write access to the repository can force push to a branch.

allow_fork_sync.description: Users can pull changes from upstream when the branch is locked.

allow_review_bypass.description: Specific users, teams, or apps can bypass pull request requirements.

allow_self_approval.description: Users can approve their own pull requests.

dismiss_stale_approvals.description: Approving reviews are automatically dismissed when someone pushes a new commit.

enforce_admins.description: All configured restrictions are also enforced for administrators.

linear_history.description: Linear commit Git history is enforced, which prevents anyone from pushing merge commits to a branch.

require_code_owner_approval.description: Pull request merges are blocked until code owners have reviewed.

require_comment_resolution.description: All pull request comments must be resolved before it can be merged.

require_status_checks.description: All status checks must pass before merging.

require_update.description: Branch must be up to date before merging.

restrict_dismiss.description: Specific users, teams, and apps can dismiss pull request reviews.

restrict_push.description: Specific users, teams, and apps can push code.

num_approvals_required.description: A minimum number of approvals is required to merge a pull request.

v1BranchAccess.description: BranchAccess contains normalized branch protection settings.

ingested_object.description: Raw ingested branch protection rule object.

v1BranchProtection.description: The list of branch protection rules for protected branches.

v1BreakdownDimension.description:
BreakdownDimension represents the dimension by which contributor usage can be broken down.

 - BREAKDOWN_DIMENSION_PROJECT: Breakdown by project.
 - BREAKDOWN_DIMENSION_USER_TYPE: Breakdown by user type (eg by bot vs human).
 - BREAKDOWN_DIMENSION_REF_TYPE: Breakdown by ref type (eg default branch vs non-default branch).
 - BREAKDOWN_DIMENSION_EMAIL_DOMAIN: Breakdown by email domain.
 - BREAKDOWN_DIMENSION_EMAIL_VERIFICATION: Breakdown by contributor email verification status (e.g. verified vs unverified).

dimension.description: The dimension at which the breakdown is performed.

dimension_key.description: The key of the breakdown dimension (e.g. project UUID).

dimension_count.description: The number of active contributors at this breakdown dimension.

metadata.description:
Additional metadata for the breakdown entry.
Keys must match pattern: ^[-A-Za-z0-9_.]*$ and be max 64 characters.
Values must be max 16384 bytes.

emails.description: The emails of the contributors at this breakdown dimension.

v1BreakdownEntry.description: BreakdownEntry represents a single breakdown dimension for contributor history.

v1BucketGranularity.description:
BucketGranularity identifies the time granularity of an aggregate bucket.

 - BUCKET_GRANULARITY_DAILY: Bucket spans a full UTC calendar day (truncated to 00:00:00Z).

uuid.description: The UUID of a CI run.

tenant_meta.description: CI runs are associated with a tenant.

spec.description: The internal specification of the object.

v1CIRun.description: Represents the information captured from a CI run of endorctl.

start_time.description: Start time is the time a CI run started.

end_time.description: End time is the time a CI run ended.

run_tags.description: The tags associated with this CI run.

baseline.description: Baseline repository version for this CI run.

v1CallGraphAnalysisType.description:
Call graph analysis type for findings.

 - CALL_GRAPH_ANALYSIS_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified call graph analysis type.
 - CALL_GRAPH_ANALYSIS_TYPE_FULL: Full call graph analysis was performed.
 - CALL_GRAPH_ANALYSIS_TYPE_PRECOMPUTED: Precomputed call graph analysis was used.

uuid.description: The UUID for a call graph resource.

meta.description: Metadata is generic for any object.

tenant_meta.description: Namespaces are associated with a tenant.

zstd_bytes.description:
Callgraph proto bytes are encoded in zstd bytes.
The caller is responsible to compress/uncompress the bytes.

any.description:
Callgraph is encoded in json bytes.
Use the HTTP header x-callgraph-encoding=any to get the spec in this format.

related_object.description: An internal value that identifies the callgraph storage location.

context.description:
The context of the call graph that is equal to the context of the associated
package.

storage_url.description: The URL of the storage location of the callgraph.

v1CallGraphData.description: CallGraphData represents a call graph data request in the system.

priority.description:
The priority of Cargo.
Priorities are relative. If multiple package managers
have the same priority, the order between them can be random.
Lower number means higher priority.

url.description: The url of the crates registry that Cargo must use.

token.description: A token that must be provided by the repository owner.

v1CargoSpec.description: CargoSpec represents a configuration for Cargo.

centered_score.description:
Centered score for the category. This score is
normalized to be centered on 5 and is a float, so it has a higher resolution.

raw_score.description:
Raw score for the category. This is the score by
adding up the score factors, not centered around 5.

v1CategoryScore.description:
The score for one score category. The is the overall score
for a specific category. It is computed from the score factors that
have been created for the category. There is going to be only a single
instance of this information for the repo per score category.

Example:

Category: SCORE_CATEGORY_BEST_PRACTICES

Score: 5

Description: This score provides an overview of how this repo does when considering security best practices.

The value is a number in the range 1 to 10, with 10 being the best.

runner_environment.description: Specifies whether the build took place in platform-hosted cloud infrastructure or customer/self-hosted infrastructure.

source_repository.description: Source repository on which the build was based.

source_repository_digest.description: Immutable reference to a specific version of the source code on which the build was based.

source_repository_owner.description: Source repository owner of the source repository on which the build was based.

source_repository_ref.description: Source Repository Ref on which the build run was based.

build_config_name.description: Name of the top-level/initiating build instructions (workflow).

build_config_digest.description: Immutable reference to the specific version of the top-level/initiating build instructions (workflow SHA).

certificate_identity.description: Immutable reference to the specific identity expected in a valid certificate. Valid values include email address, DNS names, IP addresses, and URIs.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description: Immutable reference to the specific OIDC issuer expected in a valid certificate. For example, https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com or https://oauth2.sigstore.dev/auth.

v1CertificateExtensions.description: CertificateExtensions contains the certificate extensions retrieved from an identity token.

uuid.description: The UUID of a certificate request.

meta.description: Metadata are generic for any object.

tenant_meta.description: Tenant metadata required for certificate requests.

v1CertificateRequest.description: CertificateRequest represents a certificate signing request.

type.description: The type of request.

extensions.description: Certificate extensions for image signing operations.

value.description: A string representation (base64 encoded) of the SHA/MD5 checksum of the package.

algorithm.description: Algorithm can be from MD5, SHA256, SHA1, or others.

v1Checksum.description: The details of checksum including the algorithm used to prepare the checksum.

name.description: Tool name.

categories.description: List of control function categories (based on static name to category mapping).

evidence.description: Details of where and/or how the tool was discovered.

v1CiCdTools.description: CiCdTools Metric Value contains information about CI/CD tools discovered in the repository version.

v1CisCategory.description:
CisCategory represents a CIS benchmark requirement category per
CIS Software Supply Chain Security - Base v1.0.0
https://workbench.cisecurity.org/benchmarks/7555.

v1CisReqId.description:
CisReqId represents a CIS benchmark requirement per
CIS Software Supply Chain Security - Base v1.0.0
https://workbench.cisecurity.org/benchmarks/7555.

v1CisScorecard.description:
CisScorecard represents the CIS benchmark scorecard for the parent repository.
A scorecard contains a list of benchmarks.

v1CisSubCategory.description:
CisSubCategory represents a CIS benchmark requirement sub-category per
CIS Software Supply Chain Security - Base v1.0.0
https://workbench.cisecurity.org/benchmarks/7555.

name.description: Fully qualified name of the class.

checksum.description: Checksum of the resource, used to verify data integrity.

non_metadata_checksum.description:
Checksum of the resource without any naming metadata.
Example: For Java, this is the checksum of the class file after we have
removed all occurences of namespaces (package names).

v1Class.description:
Contains metadata information about the source code for a specific Java
class.

uuid.description: The UUID of the client log.

tenant_meta.description: Namespace of the message that is accessed.

v1ClientLog.description: ClientLog represents a CRUD operation on a message.

json_payload.description: The json payload of the message.

tags.description: The tags that are associated with the log message.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the log message.

log_messages.description: An array of log messages provided as JSON payloads.

source.description: The source that is creating this message.

tool_input.description: Tool invocation input; structure is tool-specific (use Struct for JSON).

tool_response.description: Tool result; structure is tool-specific (e.g. stdout/stderr or filenames).

v1CmdHook.description: CmdHook contains payload for command-line related hooks.

patterns.description: Patterns to match against the command (e.g. "rm -rf /.*", "curl .* \\| bash").

v1CmdLineActivity.description: CmdLineActivity matches command-line execution by regex patterns.

command_source.description: Which hook payload the evaluated command text came from.

mcp_server_name.description:
MCP server that carried the command (e.g. "workspace"). Set only when
command_source is COMMAND_SOURCE_MCP_TOOL_INPUT.

tool_name.description:
MCP tool that carried the command (e.g. "bash"). Set only when
command_source is COMMAND_SOURCE_MCP_TOOL_INPUT.

v1CmdLineMatch.description: CmdLineMatch describes a command-line invocation that matched a policy.

priority.description:
The priority of the Cocoapod package manager.
Priorities are relative. If multiple package managers
have the same priority, the order between them can be random.
Lower number means higher priority.

url.description: The URL of the registry that the Cocoapods package manager must use.

v1CocoapodSpec.description:
Represents a configuration for the Cocoapod package manager.
Cocoapods does not support any registry authentication.

v1CodeOwnerData.description: Code owner information for a file path or pattern.

uuid.description: The UUID of the object.

tenant_meta.description: Tenant data.

v1CodeOwners.description: Code owner information for a project.

patterns.description:
Map of code owner data indexed by file path or pattern.

The list of owners is refreshed based on the content of
the CODEOWNERS file from the default repository version,
if present. Other fields, such as the list of labels,
can be populated manually as needed.
For projects that do not use a standard CODEOWNERS file the
entire map can be populated manually.

For more information please see the GitHub CODEOWNERS syntax.

Note:
If there is one owner for files under e.g. /src/typescript/ and
a different owner for all *.js files, then all js files under
src/typescript/ are mapped to both owners instead of basing it
on the order of the patterns in the CODEOWNERS file where the
last matching pattern takes the most precedence.

version.description:
Version the current CODEOWNERS content was first observed in.
Only updated when the CODEOWNERS file content changes.

file_hash.description: The SHA-256 hash of the CODEOWNERS file.

v1ColumnTypes.description:
The supported data types.

 - COLUMN_TYPES_UNSPECIFIED: EMPTY
 - COLUMN_TYPES_INT32: INT32
 - COLUMN_TYPES_STRING: String
 - COLUMN_TYPES_FLOAT: Float
 - COLUMN_TYPES_BOOL: Bool
 - COLUMN_TYPES_STRING_LIST: List of strings

v1ColumnValue.description:
The container for various data types that can be contained in a column.
The information from column_types in TableDescription is used to read the values.

priority.description:
The priority of the Conan package manager.
Priorities are relative. If multiple package managers
have the same priority, the order between them can be random.
Lower number means higher priority.

url.description: The URL of the Conan remote registry.

remote_name.description: The logical name of the remote in the Conan client configuration.

basic_auth.description: Basic auth credentials for the Conan remote.

aws.description: AWS authentication for the Conan remote (for example CodeArtifact).

v1ConanSpec.description: Represents a configuration for the Conan package manager.

username.description: Username for basic auth (JFrog Artifactory or self-hosted).

password.description: Password or API token for basic auth.

current.description: The current version of the direct dependency being upgraded.

upgrade.description: The new version of the direct dependency being upgraded.

conflicting_current.description: The conflicting transitive dependency, current version.

conflicting_upgrade.description: The conflicting transitive dependency, version after the upgrade.

conflicting_directs_current.description: The direct dependencies using the conflicting transitive dependency in the current version.

conflicting_directs_upgrade.description: The direct dependencies using the conflicting transitive dependency after the upgrade.

v1ContainerArchitecture.description:
Container architecture.

 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_UNKNOWN: Unknown architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_AMD64: amd64 (64-bit x86) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_386: 386 (32-bit x86) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_ARM: arm (32-bit ARM) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_ARM64: arm64 (64-bit ARM) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_PPC64LE: ppc64le (PowerPC 64-bit, little-endian) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_PPC64: ppc64 (PowerPC 64-bit, big-endian) architecture  .
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_MIPS64LE: mips64le (MIPS 64-bit, little-endian) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_MIPS64: mips64 (MIPS 64-bit, big-endian) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_MIPSLE: mipsle (MIPS 32-bit, little-endian) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_MIPS: mips (MIPS 32-bit, big-endian) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_S390X: s390x (IBM System z 64-bit, big-endian) architecture.
 - CONTAINER_ARCHITECTURE_WASM: wasm (WebAssembly 32-bit) architecture.

used.description: True if this image is used as a base image elsewhere.

use_count.description:
Number of times this image has been seen used as a base image.
This number is used for trending and it's not meant for exact usage tracking.

first_seen.description: First time this image was seen used as a base image.

last_seen.description: Most recent time this image was seen used as a base image.

update_options.description:
Update options capturing possible base image update candidates.
The update_time on ContainerImageUpdateOptions applies to the entire set of options.

v1ContainerAsBase.description: ContainerAsBase captures usage of this container image as a base image elsewhere.

name.description: The name of the base image. For example, "debian:bookworm-slim".

digest.description: The SHA256 digest of the base image.

chain_id.description: Chain ID for the base image's layers.

update_options.description: Base image update candidates for this app image.

package_version_uuid.description:
The UUID of the base image's own PackageVersion, if it has been scanned.
Populated by the scanner from the in-memory base image lookup at scan
time; consumers that need this after the fact and find it unset may fall
back to a digest-based PackageVersion lookup.

v1ContainerBaseImage.description: The base image of a container Image.

uuid.description: The UUID of the query.

tenant_meta.description: The query is scoped to a tenant.

v1ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuery.description:
ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuery computes, on demand, how the vulnerability
findings of a scanned container image's base image would change if the base
were moved to each of its available update options (refreshed, next, latest).
It is a computed query in the style of DashboardSummaryQuery: the response is
derived live from existing Finding and PackageVersion records and is never
persisted, so it cannot go stale as findings are recomputed.

v1ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuerySpe.description: Spec carries the request and the computed response.

package_version_uuid.description:
The scanned application image PackageVersion whose
container_metadata.base_image.update_options define the candidates to
assess. Its own findings supply the reachability that is projected onto
the base image findings, since candidate base scans do not measure
reachability themselves.

max_top_records_per_bucket.description:
Maximum number of top changed findings per list, in both the
severity_records and reachability_records groupings. Applied to each
bucket's fixed and introduced lists separately (e.g. up to this many
fixed and this many introduced criticals). Unset defaults to 10; set to 0
to omit the inline lists (counts only, cheaper). Capped at 100; for a full
per-bucket list use ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQueryService. A
single-digit value is typical (cf. the dashboard's top-N of 8).

record_scope.description:
Which finding types to include in the record-level fixed/introduced
lists. Unset defaults to ALL (every finding type). Only affects the
record lists (and the per-bucket *_num_results totals); the count fields
are always computed for both all and vulnerability findings.

v1ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactQuerySpe.description: Inputs that select the app image and shape the computation.

base_image_name.description:
The current base image reference (tag), copied from the app image's
container_metadata.base_image.name.

base_image_digest.description:
The current base image manifest digest, copied from the app image's
container_metadata.base_image.digest.

reachability_available.description:
True when OS reachability analysis was enabled and succeeded on the app
image scan. When true, the *_reachability_counts fields (here and on each
update option) are populated; when false they are left unset and only the
*_counts severity breakdowns are returned.

all_reachability_counts.description:
Reachability breakdown of ALL current-base findings (every finding type).
Populated only when reachability_available is true.

vuln_reachability_counts.description:
Reachability breakdown of current-base VULNERABILITY findings only.
Populated only when reachability_available is true.

all_counts.description:
Severity counts of ALL current-base findings (every finding type). Always
populated: the baseline is derived from the app image's own base-layer
findings (see §7.1), so it is available whenever update options exist.

vuln_counts.description:
Severity counts of current-base VULNERABILITY findings only. Always
populated: the baseline is derived from the app image's own base-layer
findings (see §7.1), so it is available whenever update options exist.

refreshed_option.description:
Impact of adopting the refreshed base (same tag, newer digest). Unset
when the app image has no refreshed update option.

next_option.description:
Impact of adopting the next base (the immediately newer tag by
semver/timestamp ordering). Unset when the app image has no next update
option.

v1ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQ.description:
ContainerBaseImageUpdateImpactRecordsQuery pages through the full fixed or
introduced finding list for a single update option and a single bucket (one
severity or one reachability bucket), using the standard ListParameters
pagination contract. It backs each per-bucket "View more" in the impact UI.
The impact query above returns only the top-N inline records per bucket; this
query is the drill-down for the complete per-bucket, per-kind set.

A severity bucket to page (the severity view).

 - SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED: The severity was not set.
 - SEVERITY_CRITICAL: Critical-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_HIGH: High-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_MEDIUM: Medium-severity findings.
 - SEVERITY_LOW: Low-severity findings.
Spec carries the request and the computed page of records.

list_parameters.description:
Standard pagination parameters. page_token is a numeric offset into the
fixed, total ordering (primary rank per the selected view, then a
deterministic tiebreaker of finding identity, dependency package name,
finding uuid); the handler computes the full ordered list and returns the
slice [page_token, page_token+page_size). page_size defaults to 100, max
500. filter/sort/group are ignored. next_page_token is page_token +
len(returned), unset on the last page.

v1ContributorIdentityMapping.description:
ContributorIdentityMapping links a SCM login to one or more normalized commit emails for a tenant.
Data is populated from SCM APIs (e.g. App based scans or PAT-backed reports) and used to deduplicate contributors across emails.

Deterministic canonical_email (persisted in spec.canonical_email, applied on create/update only):
 1. Normalize every associated email: trim ASCII whitespace and lowercase (same rules as contributor aggregation).
 2. Deduplicate, then sort lexicographically before persisting associated_emails.
 3. If any email is a GitHub noreply address for this login (see github.com docs: USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com
    or ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com), pick the lexicographically smallest matching noreply address.
 4. Otherwise use the lexicographically smallest normalized email.

Aggregation and other readers must use spec.canonical_email as stored;
they must not re-derive a different "first" email from scan order.

v1EndorIgnoreEntry.description:
Represents a single entry in the ignore file.

EndorIgnoreEntry objects are created by the endorctl client after
reading and processing the ignore file during the git scan,
and then applied to the findings during the analytics scan.

The ignore file is either a raw list of vulnerability ids
(one per line), or a YAML file that contains a list of ignore entries,
each identifying one or more findings in a repository version.
The file is formatted manually or via the endorctl ignore command.

Each entry must specify at least the finding name or the vulnerability ID.
The more fields you provide, the more specific the ignore entry is.
I.e. if you only provide the finding name and there are multiple
findings with the same name in the same repository version,
the ignore entry is applied to all of them.
Use the endorctl ignore --finding-uuid option to automatically populate
all fields of the ignore entry based on a given finding.

ignore_params.description: Metadata associated with the ignore entry.

finding_name.description:
Name of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "Potential secret leak Generic API Key: ID #3b0fbc".
Exact matches only.

Please note that finding names are stored in the meta.description
field of the finding object rather than in meta.name.
Yes, this is confusing, but there are historical reasons for this.

parent_name.description:
Name of the parent of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "com.endor.webapp:endor-java-webapp-demo@4.0-SNAPSHOT".
Partial matches are accepted.

This corresponds to the meta.name field of the parent object
pointed to by the meta.parent_uuid field of the finding object.

dependency_name.description:
Name of the dependency of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core@2.3".
Partial matches are accepted.

This corresponds to the spec.target_dependency_package_name field
of the finding object for PackageVersion findings.

vuln_id.description:
Vulnerability ID of the finding that is being ignored.
For example, "CVE-2025-12345" or "GHSA-7rjr-3q55-vv33".
Exact matches only.

extra_key.description:
Extra key for the finding that is being ignored.
For example, the finding policy UUID.
Exact matches only.

The extra key is used internally to uniquely identify findings
(along with other fields such as the parent, target, and type)
and is stored in the spec.extra_key field of the finding object.

customer success reporting.

Format: Salesforce IDs are either 15 or 18 characters:
- 15 chars: case-sensitive alphanumeric (0-9, a-z, A-Z)
- 18 chars: 15-char ID + 3-char case-safe checksum
Pattern validates format only, not checksum correctness.
Ref: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9742913/validating-a-salesforce-id

v1EndorctlRC.description:
Endorctl return codes.

 - ENDORCTL_RC_SUCCESS: Success (translates to exit code 0).
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ERROR: Unspecified error.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_INVALID_ARGS: Invalid input.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ENDOR_AUTH_FAILURE: Endor API authentication failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DOCTOR_FAILURE: Endor host-check failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GITHUB_AUTH_FAILURE: GitHub authentication failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ANALYTICS_ERROR: Error running analytics.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_FINDINGS_ERROR: Error generating findings.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_NOTIFICATIONS_ERROR: Error generating notifications.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GITHUB_API_ERROR: Error calling GitHub API.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GITHUB_PERMISSIONS_ERROR: Insufficient GitHub token permissions.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GIT_ERROR: Error while performing a Git operation.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEPENDENCY_RESOLUTION_ERROR: Error during dependency resolution.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEPENDENCY_SCANNING_ERROR: Error during dependency scanning.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CALL_GRAPH_ERROR: Error while generating call graphs.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_LINTER_ERROR: Error while running the linter scanner.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_BAD_POLICY_TYPE: A user defined policy has a policy type reserved for system policies.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_POLICY_ERROR: Error evaluating one or more policies.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_INTERNAL_ERROR: Internal error while running endorctl.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: Deadline exceeded while running endorctl.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_NOT_FOUND: Requested entity was not found.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ALREADY_EXISTS: Attempt to create an entity failed because it already exists.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_UNAUTHENTICATED: Unable to authenticate request.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_VULN_ERROR: Error related to vulnerability ingestion and processing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_INITIALIZATION_ERROR: Error related to initializing the repository.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_HOST_CHECK_FAILURE: Endor host-check failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SBOM_IMPORT_ERROR: Error importing an sbom.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_PRE_COMMIT_CHECK_FAILURE: A pre-commit check failed.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_GH_ACTION_WORKFLOW_SCAN_FAILURE: GitHub action workflow scan failed.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_FILE_ANALYTICS_ERROR: Error while reading files for analytics processing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION_FAILURE: Signature verification failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_LICENSE_ERROR: The requested operation requires additional licensing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_HUGGING_FACE_ERROR: Error while running the huggingface scanner.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SAST_ERROR: Error while running the SAST scanner.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_ARTIFACT_OPERATION_FAILURE: Artifact operation failure.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SEGMENTATION_ERROR: Error during file segmentation.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_TOOLCHAIN_ERROR: Error generating toolchains.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SANDBOX_ERROR: Error running endorctl sandbox.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_RULE_SET_ERROR: Error performing rule set operations.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SECURITY_REVIEW_ERROR: Error while running the PR security review.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CODE_API_ERROR: Error while running codeAPI.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_BASELINE_NOT_FOUND: Baseline is invalid or has not been scanned yet.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_SCAN_CANCELLED: Scan was cancelled.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_POLICY_VIOLATION: One or more, enforced, admission policy violations detected.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_POLICY_WARNING: One ore more, unenforced, admission policy violations detected.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_PR_SECURITY_REVIEW_ERROR: Deprecated: Use ENDORCTL_RC_SECURITY_REVIEW_ERROR instead.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_EXPORTER_WARNING: Warning while running the exporter. This does not prevent the main scan
from completing.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_CONTAINER_PROFILING_WARNING: Warning while profiling a container image.
 - ENDORCTL_RC_DEPENDENCY_SETUP_WARNING: Warning during dependency environment setup (e.g. truststore creation).
The scan continues with a fallback configuration but may encounter issues.

A finding contains details of a problem that needs to be fixed.
The finding applies to the parent object, which can be one of:
Repository, RepositoryVersion, or PackageVersion.
Finding objects are connected to the project via spec.project_uuid.

v1FindingCategory.description:
Finding categories loosely correspond to use cases.

 - FINDING_CATEGORY_VULNERABILITY: Vulnerability.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SUPPLY_CHAIN: Supply chain specific problem (malicious packages, typosquats).
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_LICENSE_RISK: License issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SCPM: Security posture management.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SECURITY: Generic security issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_OPERATIONAL: Generic operational issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SECRETS: Exposed secret.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_MALWARE: Malware.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_CICD: CI/CD pipeline issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_TOOLS: Tooling issue.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_GHACTIONS: Finding applies to a GitHub action dependency.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_CONTAINER: Finding applies to a container image.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SAST: SAST.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_AI_MODELS: AI Models.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SECURITY_REVIEW: Security review.
 - FINDING_CATEGORY_SCA: Software Composition Analysis issue.

v1FindingClassification.description:
Classification of the finding type. Extensible for future categories.

 - FINDING_CLASSIFICATION_SECURITY_VULNERABILITY: Security vulnerability (e.g. SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded creds).
 - FINDING_CLASSIFICATION_LOGICAL_BUG: Logical bug (e.g. null pointer, resource leak, race condition).

List of layer digests for the container image where the target

Set to true if the target dependency was found in the base layer of the
container image.

group.description: The group whose criteria the counted findings match.

counts.description: Severity breakdown of the findings left at this stage.

v1FindingCountEntry.description:
Counts for one stage of one group.
An entry is emitted only where the group matched at least one finding, so a missing entry reads
as zero rather than as absent data.

v1FindingCountGroup.description:
Identifies a group: a set of finding-matching criteria, and a tree of stages that narrows it.
Both the criteria and the stage tree live in the backend registry, which is the only emitter of
these counts. Groups are not mutually exclusive, so a finding matching two of them would be
counted in each.

 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_UNSPECIFIED: No group has been set.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_SCA_VULNERABILITY: Findings carrying both the SCA and vulnerability categories.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_AI_SAST: Findings carrying the SAST category and the AI tag.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_SECRETS: Findings carrying the secrets category.
 - FINDING_COUNT_GROUP_CONTAINER: Findings carrying the container category.

v1FindingCountStage.description:
Identifies one step in a group's stage tree.
Each value names only the criteria that step narrows by. A stage counts what is left once its own
criteria and every criteria on its path from the tree's root have been applied, so the same stage
counts a different set in each group it appears in, and the registry's stage tree is the only
place a stage's full criteria can be read. Sibling stages fork the funnel: each narrows their
shared parent independently, and their sets may overlap.

 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_UNSPECIFIED: No stage has been set.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_TOTAL: Narrows by nothing; counts every finding matching the group's own criteria.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_NOT_IN_TEST: Narrows to findings carrying the normal tag, which marks findings outside test code.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_FIX_AVAILABLE: Narrows to findings carrying the fix available tag.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_REACHABLE: Narrows to findings carrying the reachable function tag for SCA vulnerabilities, or the
reachable dependency tag for containers.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_EXPLOITABLE: Narrows to findings with an EPSS probability at or above 1%, the threshold for exploitation in
the wild. Follows REACHABLE in every group that uses it, so it never counts an unreachable
finding.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_TRUE_POSITIVE: Narrows to findings carrying the true positive tag.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_VALID_SECRET: Narrows to findings carrying the valid secret tag, set when the secret still authenticates
against its provider.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE: Narrows to findings carrying a potentially reachable tag. Forks from the same parent as
REACHABLE, and the two branches may overlap: a finding tagged both reachable and potentially
reachable is counted in each.
 - FINDING_COUNT_STAGE_POTENTIALLY_EXPLOITABLE: Narrows by the same EPSS threshold as EXPLOITABLE, but follows POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE, so it
counts the exploitable findings on the potentially reachable branch.

v1FindingRecordScope.description:
Which finding types populate the record-level fixed/introduced lists. Shared
by the impact query and the records drill-down query. The severity/reachability

selects only which findings appear in the record lists and, correspondingly,
which totals those record views reconcile against.

 - FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED: Unset; treated as FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_ALL.
 - FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_ALL: All finding types. Record views reconcile with all_counts / all_changes.
 - FINDING_RECORD_SCOPE_VULNERABILITY: Vulnerability findings only. Record views reconcile with vuln_counts /
vuln_changes.

 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_UPGRADE: Upgrade to a later version.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_DOWNGRADE: Downgrade to an older version.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REPLACE: Replace dependency with another package.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REMOVE: Remove unused dependency.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_VENDOR: Vendor a dependency.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_IMPROVE: Make changes to improve a dependency.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REIMPLEMENT: Reimplement a dependency locally.
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_REVIEW: Review, no remediation to suggest
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_NOTIFICATION: Notification, there may not be any remediation
 - FINDING_REMEDIATION_PIN: Pin dependency to one of the recommended versions

v1FindingTags.description:
Finding attributes.

 - FINDING_TAGS_DIRECT: Finding applies to a direct dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_TRANSITIVE: Finding applies to a transitive (indirect) dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PROJECT_INTERNAL: Finding applies to a dependency that belongs to the same project.
 - FINDING_TAGS_NAMESPACE_INTERNAL: Finding applies to a dependency that belongs to the same namespace.
 - FINDING_TAGS_REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY: Finding applies to a reachable dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNREACHABLE_DEPENDENCY: Finding applies to an unreachable dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY: Finding applies to a potentially reachable dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_REACHABLE_FUNCTION: Finding applies to a reachable function.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNREACHABLE_FUNCTION: Finding applies to an unreachable function.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE_FUNCTION: Finding applies to a potentially reachable function.
 - FINDING_TAGS_FIXABLE: Deprecated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNFIXABLE: Finding is unfixable.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PRODUCTION: Deprecated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_TEST: Finding applies to a dependency not in production code.
 - FINDING_TAGS_NORMAL: Finding applies to a normal, non-test, dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_FIX_AVAILABLE: There is a fix available for the CVE reported in this finding.
 - FINDING_TAGS_SELF: Finding applies only to the analyzed package version, there is no
dependency involved.
 - FINDING_TAGS_POLICY: Deprecated.
 - FINDING_TAGS_CI_BLOCKER: Finding caused a CI failure.
 - FINDING_TAGS_VALID_SECRET: Finding applies to a valid secret.
 - FINDING_TAGS_INVALID_SECRET: Finding applies to an invalid secret.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PATH_EXTERNAL: Finding applies to a transitive dependency that can only be reached via
external, non-OSS, project paths.
 - FINDING_TAGS_MALWARE: Finding applies to malicious package.
 - FINDING_TAGS_UNDER_REVIEW: Finding applies to suspicious package under review.
 - FINDING_TAGS_PHANTOM: Finding applies to a phantom dependency.
 - FINDING_TAGS_EXCEPTION: Finding is exempt from action policies.
 - FINDING_TAGS_CI_WARNING: Finding caused a CI warning.
 - FINDING_TAGS_NOTIFICATION: Finding triggered a notification.
 - FINDING_TAGS_EXPLOITED: This vulnerability is known to be exploited.
 - FINDING_TAGS_DISPUTED: This vulnerability has been marked as 'disputed'.
 - FINDING_TAGS_WITHDRAWN: This vulnerability has been marked as 'withdrawn'.
 - FINDING_TAGS_FALSE_POSITIVE: This finding has been analyzed to be a false positive.
 - FINDING_TAGS_TRUE_POSITIVE: This finding has been analyzed to be a true positive.
 - FINDING_TAGS_SNOOZED: Finding has been snoozed.
 - FINDING_TAGS_AI: This finding was generated using AI.
 - FINDING_TAGS_IGNORED: Finding has been ignored via the ignore file.
 - FINDING_TAGS_SEGMENT_MATCH: Finding applies to a dependency discovered via segment-matching.

v1FunctionSummaryHashesQuery.description:
FunctionSummaryHashesQuery reports which of the given segment hashes are

version or newer. Unlike FunctionSummaryQuery, which returns full summary
content and only matches usable ('ok') summaries for search consumers,
this checks bare existence so a client can skip re-summarizing a segment
already tombstoned as trivial or failed.
