http_clone_url.description:
The HTTP clone URL.

The following examples show valid URLs.

https://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git

http://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git

https://my.github.com/a/b.git

https://www.gitlab.com/a/b/c.git

https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x.git

https://github.com/jboss/jboss-ejb-api_spec.git

The URL is stored as lower case letters to normalize searches.

git_clone_url.description:
The Git clone URL.
For example, git://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git.

The URL is stored as lower case letters to normalize searches.

organization.description:
The organization where the repository is located.

For example, yarpc

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq
.organization.login

path.description:
The source control repository in the project without the organization.

For example, yarpc-go

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq .name

full_name.description:
Represents the Git namespace and its associated hierarchy.

The format is "namespace/name", comprising the organization name and
repository name.

For example, yarpc/yarpc-go

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq .full_name

web_url.description:
The web URL to view the repository.

For example, https://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go

GitHub: curl https://api.github.com/repos/yarpc/yarpc-go | jq .html_url

The URL is stored as lower case letters to normalize searches.

template_params.title:

in the vicinity of the secret for validation. Each entry represents a set of values that can be
tried in sequence during validation.
Example: [{"values": [{"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_CLIENT_ID", "value": "abc123"}, {"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_TENANT_ID", "value": "xyz789"}]}]

allowed_template_params.title:
AllowedTemplateParams defines a list of allowed template parameter names and regexes for validating their values.
Only the template parameters with names in this list will be allowed in the template_params field.
Example: [{"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_CLIENT_ID", "regex": "abc[0-9]{3}"}, {"name": "TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_TENANT_ID", "regex": "xyz[0-9]{3}"}]

with matching values. The response can contain additional fields.

The expected response body text for successful validation.
Example: "invalid_payload" would require the response body to contain the text "invalid_payload".
The response body may contain additional text.

v1InventoryAdminClassification.description:
InventoryAdminClassification carries the allow/block axis plus evidence.
Within a single event, when multiple matching policies disagree, the
stronger value wins (BLOCKED dominates ALLOWED dominates UNSPECIFIED).
Across events, the current policy set is authoritative: a later event
that no longer matches any classification policy leaves the field
untouched, but a later event matching a different policy reclassifies
the record accordingly.

v1InventoryClassification.description:
InventoryClassification declares the classification a policy assigns to a
matched MCP server or skill when it fires. UNSPECIFIED means the policy
plays no role in inventory classification (e.g. a session, file-access,
or cmd-line policy, or an MCP/skill policy whose author only wants the
per-event action).

policy_name.description: Policy name at the time of match (snapshot — not refreshed later).

v1InventoryClassificationEvidence.description:
InventoryClassificationEvidence records the policy that assigned the
current value on a single classification axis. Snapshotted from the
matching AgentHookPolicy so the inventory record remains self-describing
after the policy is renamed or deleted.

evidence.description: Evidence describing the policy that assigned the current value.

v1InventoryThreatClassification.description:
InventoryThreatClassification carries the suspicious/malicious axis plus
evidence. Within a single event, when multiple matching policies disagree,
the stronger value wins (MALICIOUS dominates SUSPICIOUS dominates
UNSPECIFIED). Across events, the current policy set is authoritative:
see InventoryAdminClassification for the full semantics.

LicenseMappingInfo contains additional information
that we determine when we attempt to match a license string
to a known SPDX id.

 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_NOT_OSS: This does not look to like an OSS license.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_IN_CODE: License information is to be found in the code.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_UNKNOWN: Cannot determine anything about the license.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_NOT_INCOMPLETE: There is some license information, but is not detailed enough.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_PRIVATE: Appears to be a private package.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_EXACT: An exact match to a SPDX id.
 - LICENSE_MAPPING_INFO_UNLICENSED: Seems to be explicitly without license.

filter.description:
String of conditions to filter resources by.
Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

v1MalwareExposure.description:
Namespace exposure for a given Malware package.
The presence of this object indicates that at least one project in the
Namespace is, or was, potentially affected by the referenced Malware.
If all affected projects are in child namespaces, then there are no
MalwareExposure objects in the parent namespace. Use traverse to
include MalwareExposure objects from child namespaces.
The meta.name field contains the fully qualified package name of the
Malware package. For example, "npm://package-name".

malware_uuids.description:
UUIDs of the Malware objects to get exposure for.
Leave empty to get exposure for all, non-contested Malware objects.
Use the filter field to get exposure for a subset of Malware
objects if you do not have the UUIDs.

Note: The UUIDs are not checked for existence.
There is no error returned if a UUID is not found, but there
will not be an entry for it in the project counts.

filter.description:
String of conditions to filter MalwareExposure objects by.
For example, to only get data for the last 7 days, use:
"meta.create_time >= now(-168h)".

Only applied if malware_uuids is empty.
Skips contested malware records.

Note: The filter is applied to the MalwareExposure objects,
not the Malware objects.

Filters may include any attribute along with the following operators:
"==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<=", "Contains", "In", "Matches", and
"Exists". The logical operators "And" and "Or" are also supported.
Expressions may be combined and grouped with parentheses.

Examples:
"spec.value == 5",
"spec.value in ["a", "b", "c"]",
"(meta.name == "xyz" and "spec.value in ["a","b"]) or (spec.value ==
"c")".

traverse.description: Get data from any child namespaces as well.

v1MalwareWorkflowLLMConfigThinkingLevel.description:
ThinkingLevel controls the depth of reasoning a model applies before producing a response.

 - THINKING_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED: No thinking level has been set; the model uses its default behavior.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_AUTO: The model selects the appropriate thinking depth automatically.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_LOW: Minimal reasoning; faster and cheaper, suited for straightforward signals.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_MEDIUM: Moderate reasoning; balanced between quality and cost.
 - THINKING_LEVEL_HIGH: Maximum reasoning; slower and more expensive, suited for complex verdicts.

v1McpDimensionThresholds.description:
McpDimensionThresholds holds per-dimension score thresholds for
McpServerActivity. Each field is optional; an unset dimension is ignored.
Set dimensions are OR'd among themselves and with score_at_or_below:
any single dimension at or below its threshold fires the predicate.
Dimension names mirror AgenticInventory.McpScoreDimensions.

server_name_matchers.description:
Regex matchers for MCP server name (e.g. "untrusted-.*", "remote-.*").
AND'd with the score-predicate branch when both are configured.

score_at_or_below.description:
Match when the overall score is at or below this threshold
(scores are 1-10, higher = safer). OR'd with dimension_at_or_below.

dimension_at_or_below.description:
Per-dimension score thresholds. OR'd among themselves and with
score_at_or_below.

v1McpServerActivity.description:
McpServerActivity matches MCP servers by name patterns and/or score
thresholds. Match logic: configured branches are AND'd — when both
server_name_matchers and score predicates are set, both must hold;
when only one is set, only that one must hold; if neither is set,
the activity never matches. Within the score branch, score_at_or_below
and every set field of dimension_at_or_below are OR'd: any single
satisfied threshold fires the branch. This is server-level matching;
for per-tool-call matching, use McpToolCallActivity.

mcp_server_name.description: Name of the MCP server that matched.

Describes what exactly matched (e.g. "score at or below threshold 5",

v1McpServerMatch.description:
McpServerMatch describes an MCP server that matched a policy. Carries

from AgenticInventory if more detail is needed. Server-level match;
for individual tool calls, see McpToolMatch.

  is retried in subsequent attempts. Flags are maintained for

- Metadata specific to a notification target type. Some of
  the notification target types need to maintain state so that
  subsequent updates to the notifications can operate on the
  same entity created by the notification. For example, JIRA

v1PackageFirewallAction.description:
PackageFirewallAction defines how the package firewall responds when a check is triggered.
Used in both configuration (what to do) and audit logs (what was done).

 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_ACTION_BLOCK: Block the request and return HTTP 403.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_ACTION_WARN: Log a warning audit event and allow the request to proceed.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_ACTION_CURATED: One or more versions were removed from the package metadata response as part of package curation.
The package manager resolves to the best remaining safe version without seeing the curated-out versions.

cvss_severity_level.description: CVSS severity level of the detected vulnerability (populated only when reason is CVSS_SEVERITY_DETECTED).

Per-version detail for MetadataAllVersions curation events.
Populated when package_curation_enabled = true and one or more versions were suppressed
from the metadata response because their per-policy action is BLOCK. Empty for all other request types.

v1PackageFirewallReason.description:
PackageFirewallReason represents the check that triggered the firewall event.

 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_MALWARE_DETECTED: Malware was detected in the requested package version.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_MIN_AGE_NOT_MET: The requested package version does not meet the configured minimum age.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_RESTRICTED_LICENSE: The requested package version has a license that is on the restricted list.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_CVSS_SEVERITY_DETECTED: The requested package version has a CVSS vulnerability meeting or exceeding the configured severity threshold.
 - PACKAGE_FIREWALL_REASON_VERSIONS_CURATED: One or more versions were removed from the package metadata response as part of package curation.
See PackageFirewallLog.Spec.filtered_versions for per-version detail.

v1PackageLicenseOverride.description:
PackageLicenseOverride represents user edits and selections for licenses, copyrights, and notices
at the package version level. Edits made at this level apply across all projects in the namespace
that use the same package version.
The package version UUID is stored in spec.package_version_uuid.

license_overrides.description:
Map of license identifier to LicenseOverride.
Contains licenses that have been edited or newly added by the user.
Original licenses from PackageLicense are NOT stored here - they are fetched from PackageLicense when needed.
Key format: hash calculated from normalized license text (same calculation as PackageLicenseInfo.hash).
  - For edited licenses from PackageLicense: use hash from PackageLicenseInfo.hash.
    (this hash maps to the key in PackageLicense.spec.license_text map).
  - For new licenses added by user: calculate hash from the license_text provided in LicenseOverride.
    The hash is calculated using the same method: SHA256(MakeLicenseKey(normalized_license_text)).
The hash is calculated from the normalized license text and is available for all
license types (code_licenses, package_manager_licenses, declared_code_licenses).

copyright_overrides.description:
Map of copyright key to CopyrightOverride.
Contains copyrights that have been edited or newly added by the user.
Original copyrights from PackageLicense are NOT stored here - they are fetched from PackageLicense when needed.
Key format:
  - For edited copyrights from PackageLicense: use the key from PackageLicense.spec.copyrights map.
    (this is the file path where the copyright was found).
  - For new copyrights added by user: use generated UUID prefixed with "new-".

notice_overrides.title:
Map of notice identifier to NoticeOverride.
Contains notices that have been edited or newly added by the user.
Original notices from PackageLicense are NOT stored here - they are fetched from PackageLicense when needed.
Key format:
  - For edited notices from PackageLicense: use hash or composite identifier
  - For new notices added by user: use generated UUID prefixed with "new-"

The findings are aggregated based on the aggregation type and

Set to true if exception policies should be ignored for findings
matching this policy.

Lists of UUIDs of resources that violate the policy,
if applicable, indexed by resource name.

True if input data is accepted by policy.
False if input data violates the expected state.

The policy type.
Depending on the policy type different actions might be allowed.

The policy rule in text format.

For example:

   data.resources.Project[_].meta.name = go-memdb"
}

project_selector.description:
The set of tags that projects must have for the policy to be executed
against. If left empty, the policy applies to all projects of the
namespace. The items in the array correspond to an OR operator. That is,
any project with a tag that matches any of the project_selector values
will be matched.

project_exceptions.description:
The set of tags that projects that are matched
with are excluded from the policy. Allows exceptions. Exceptions
can be provided with or without selectors.

Identifies all resources that a policy requires.
For example, "Project", "Repository", "RepositoryVersion",
"PackageVersion", "DependencyMetadata", "Metric", "LinterResult",
"Finding", etc. For the "Metric" resource you must also specify the
corresponding parent resource kind.

disable.description: Disables a policy without deleting it.

query_statements.description:
The list of OPA query statements that must be executed to evaluate the
policy. For example, [ "data.packagename.allow" ], [opulated from
template if applicable.

template_uuid.description: Indicates that the policy is created from a template.

template_values.description: The map of key-value pairs for parameters used to customize the template.

template_parameters.description: Template parameter metadata for this template version.

finding_level.description:
Corresponding finding severity level if applicable.
This field can be used to filter and/or sort policies records.
It is populated automatically by the system for all policy types
and is not used to set the severity of any findings generated
from the policy. To change the finding severity level update
the level field in the finding action message below.

group_by_fields.description:
Custom fields to group policy output by. This may be a
subset of all custom keys in the policy output. You do not need to
add all custom fields here, just the ones you want to be used to
group the matches by. The corresponding values
are always treated as a single string.

finding_categories.description:
List of finding categories that the policy creates or acts on findings
for. This field can be used to group policies.

PolicyTemplate represents a policy system in the system. Policy
templates can be used to create policies from these templates.

rule.description:
The policy template rule in text format.

For example:

package policyexample

default allow = false

allow {
   input.Value1 = input.Value2
}

template_parameters.description:
The list of values to customize the template. In the example above,
Value1 and Value2.

resource_kinds.description:
The additional resources that a policy requires.
By default, policies are executed against Project, Repository,
RepositoryVersion, PackageVersion, Metric and Finding. If a policy
must include additional objects they must be defined here.

query_statements.description:
The list of OPA query statements that must be executed to evaluate the
resulting policy. For example, [ "data.packagename.allow" ].

policy_type.description:
The type of policy that will be created.
Depending on the policy type different actions might be allowed.

default_enabled.description:
True if generated out-of-the-box policy is enabled by default
(unless Policy.AutoEnable is explicitly disabled in SystemConfig).
Default user finding policies are also generated for new tenants
if this flag is set to true.

finding_level.description:
Corresponding finding severity level if applicable.
Used to filter and/or sort policy templates.
It is populated automatically by the system for all policy types
and is not used to set the severity of any findings generated
from the policies. To change the finding severity level
update the level field in the finding action message below.

group_by_fields.description:
Custom fields to group policy output by. This may be a subset of all
custom keys in the policy output. You do not need to add all custom
fields here. You can add just the custom fileds you want to be used to
group the matches by. The corresponding values are always treated as a
single string.

release_notes.description: Release notes indexed by template version.

deprecated.description:
Set to True if the policy template has been deprecated.
Policies created from deprecated templates are never deleted,
but the template is no longer visible in the UI.

finding_categories.description:
List of finding categories that the policy creates or acts on findings
for. This field can be used to group policy templates.

PrecomputedState represents the state of precomputed operations.

 - PRECOMPUTED_STATE_UNSPECIFIED: UNSPECIFIED indicates that the precomputed state is not set or unknown.
 - PRECOMPUTED_STATE_SUCCESS: SUCCESS indicates that the precomputed operation completed successfully.

QueryMalware is used to do query request on malware that are
not supported by ListMalware and the filter. For instance, you must

Version-less package names (ecosystem://name) to look up. Unlike
package_version_name(s), each entry returns ALL malware records for the
package across every malicious version and range, rather than a single
version match. Used to detect packages that are (potentially) impacted
regardless of the resolved version, e.g. unpinned dependencies.

For example, https://github.com/yarpc/yarpc-go.git.

commit_hashes.description:
Commit hashes contains a list of all of the commit presents in the repository.

A commit hash contains all commits branches that were already ingested.

For example: with branch A, branch B and branch C, where branch A and branch B were
ingested, the array contains the union of commits of branch A and branch B.

target.description:
The target object (path or package) where the failure happened. For package
scans it is the package. For the workspace scans it is the target path.

description.description:
A description of the error. Plugins should use proper descriptions that
will be helpful to users or operations.

operation.description:
The operation during which encountered the error.
A Go plugin can return as operation reading go.mod file,
a Java plugin can be reading a pom.xml. Every plugin is
doing different operations and it should identify here
the operation that failed. This again will help with debugging.

error_analysis.description:
The analysis of the error based on the error parsing rules
that can provide additional context on possible fixes.

error_analysis_best_match.description: The best error analysis match ordered by rule priority.

target_files.description: The content of manifest files or the list of files based on the operation.

v1ResolutionStatus.description:
ResolutionStatus is the response status that indicates if the operation
succeeded. The response status will be stored with the
results. The caller will continue with subsequent requests
and the server can continue with additional packages.

v1RuleSourceType.description: The source type of the rule set.

sso_url.description: Single Sign On URL of the identity provider.

attribute_names.description: Attributes that must be mapped to the Endor identity.

kind.description:
Identifies the SBOM specification the output should conform to. Restricted
to CycloneDx (1) and SPDX (2); other SBOMKind values are rejected.

format.description:
Serialization format of the rendered SBOM document. Restricted to JSON,
XML, and Tag-Value; the format must be compatible with the chosen kind
(e.g. SPDX Tag-Value is supported, CycloneDx Tag-Value is not).

component_type.description: Library or application classification for the SBOM root component.

hide_private_components.description: Whether to hide private (internal) packages in the SBOM output.

include_test_dependencies.description:
Whether to include test/dev/build/optional dependencies. When false
(default), non-production dependencies are excluded along with any
transitive dependencies reachable only through them.

export_parameters.description:
Parameters describing which package versions to include in the SBOM.
Supports project_uuid / project_name / package_version_uuids variants.

package_version_uuid.description:
UUID of a single PackageVersion to export. When set, the handler
generates an SBOM containing just this package version. Mutually
exclusive with export_parameters.

include_vulnerabilities.description:
When true, embed the scope's vulnerabilities as a top-level
vulnerabilities[] array in the SBOM, producing one unified document.
CycloneDx only.

The file path of the generated SBOM in object storage.
Stored on the Job by the handler; the apiserver Job RPC layer reads
this on every GetJob and produces a fresh signed download URL.

report_url.description:
The signed download URL for the generated SBOM. Populated by the
apiserver Job RPC layer on each GetJob call (5-minute TTL).

sbom_size_bytes.description:
Byte length of the generated SBOM artifact in object storage. Useful
for clients deciding whether to display a download progress indicator
and for operational reporting on export sizes.

resource_namespace.description:
Namespace jobctl read the referenced resources from — the caller's
tenant, or "oss" if the fallback fired.

v1SBOMExportJobResponse.description: Response holds the output after the SBOM export job completes.

organization_urls.description: The list of URLs associated with the given organization, which can be included in the supplier SBOM information.

modules in an SBOM. Provides information about the package like name,
version, and repository location.

v1SCMCredential.description:
SCMCredential represents SCM org/repo credentials for private dependency resolution.
Customers configure these credentials to allow endorctl to authenticate with
private Git repositories during agentless or SCM-integrated scans, eliminating
resolution failures for cross-org private dependencies.

platform_source.description: The SCM platform type (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure, etc.).

target_url.description:
The target URL of the SCM org or repo for which this credential applies.
Examples:
  - Org-level:  "https://github.com/myorg"
  - Repo-level: "https://github.com/myorg/private-repo"
Git URL rewrites will be applied for all sub-paths of this URL.

access_token.description:
Access token for authenticating to the SCM platform.
Used for HTTPS-based Git operations (e.g., git URL rewrites).
Works across all SCM providers: GitHub PAT, GitLab PAT, Bitbucket access
token, Azure DevOps PAT, etc.
The secure annotation ensures automatic redaction and secure storage.

v1ScanCreditUsage.description:
ScanCreditUsage is a per-tenant snapshot of scan credit consumption produced
by the licensing aggregation job. One object is written per aggregation run
covering a fixed [period_start, period_end) window. The most recent object's
term_* fields hold cumulative usage for the current contract term anchored
at EndorLicense.spec.credits_period_start.

window_start.description:
Start of the aggregation window this snapshot covers (inclusive).
Typically equals the previous run's window_end, or term_start for the
first run of a term.

window_end.description:
End of the aggregation window this snapshot covers (exclusive). All
ScanResults with create_time in [window_start, window_end) contributed
to window_* fields.

credits_period_start.description:
Anchor timestamp of the current contract term. Snapshotted from
EndorLicense.spec.credits_period_start at aggregation time so historic
rows remain interpretable after renewal.

window_scan_credits.description:
Total credits consumed during [window_start, window_end). Sum of all
six window_breakdown counters.

cumulative_scan_credits.description:
Cumulative credits consumed since credits_period_start through
window_end. Sum of all six cumulative_breakdown counters. Used to
render remaining credits and overage in the UI without rescanning all
snapshots.

cumulative_breakdown.description:
Per-context, per-component breakdown cumulative since credits_period_start
through window_end.

scan_credit_limit.description:
Scan credit limit in effect at aggregation time. Snapshotted from
EndorLicense.spec.scan_credit_limit. Overage = max(0, cumulative_scan_credits - credit_limit).

onboarded_project_count.description:
Number of non-deleted projects onboarded under the tenant observed at
aggregation time. Used to decide whether the 5x-seats default-branch cap
was exceeded.

overflow_project_count.description:
Number of projects beyond the 5x-seats cap whose default-branch scans
contributed to *_main_overflow_credits counters. Zero when
onboarded_project_count <= 5 * seats.

v1ScanState.description:
Scan state for a project or package version.

 - SCAN_STATE_NOT_PROCESSED: Object has not been processed by the system yet.
Set when the project or package is created for the first time.
A new project or package version is automatically placed in this state.
 - SCAN_STATE_IDLE: Object has been scanned at least once.
 - SCAN_STATE_INGESTING: Object is being scanned.
 - SCAN_STATE_ANALYTIC: Object is being analyzed.
 - SCAN_STATE_UNREACHABLE: Object cannot be ingested because it is not reachable from the scheduler.
 - SCAN_STATE_REQUEST_FULL_RESCAN: Object is marked for a complete rescan.
This only applies to OSS projects.
 - SCAN_STATE_REQUEST_INCREMENTAL_RESCAN: Object is marked for an incremental rescan, where only new packages
discovered in the scan are added. Indicates that this project should be
rescanned with a higher priority. Often because it is used by a customer
and we need any new packages to be discovered and scanned with higher
priority. If the project is put in this state, we will scan any new
packages at high priority but we will not re-scan older packages.
 - SCAN_STATE_QUEUED: Object is queued to be scanned.
 - SCAN_STATE_QUARANTINED: Scan scheduling was unsuccessful due to a system errors. Object is
quarantined from additional scheduling. Potentially object is an
orphan or similar situations.

v1SchedulerResourceHistory.description:
SchedulerResourceHistory stores per-project resource usage history and sizing
recommendations for scheduler jobs. One document per (project_uuid, kind).
Written by the resource recorder on job completion; read by the launcher to
size the next run's resource requests.

v1ScopePolicy.description:
ScopePolicy represents a scope policy in the system. Scope policies allow users
to select for a set of projects (or namespaces) as defined by the project selectors.
It is the set of policies that are applied to these projects as defined by a policy selector.

project_namespace_selector.description:
The list of namespaces for which this scope rule will apply.
For example, defining a namespace "tenant" will mean that the rule applies for all
projects in the namespace.

project_tag_selector.description:
The set of tags that projects must have for the scope policy to be executed against.
If left empty, the scope policy applies to all projects of the namespace. The items in the array
correspond to an OR operator. That is, any project with a tag that matches any
of the project_selector values will be matched.

excluded_project_tag_selector.description: The set of tags that projects must not have for the scope policy to be executed against.

policy_namespace_selector.description:
Selects all policies in the namespace to be applied.
If the policy_namespace_selector is defined, the policy_tag_selector cannot be defined at the same time.

 - SCORE_CATEGORY_ACTIVITY: Tracks the amount of activity around a project.
 - SCORE_CATEGORY_BEST_PRACTICES: Tracks how much a project follows various development best practices.

 - SCORE_CATEGORY_DEPENDENCIES: Tracks the dependencies of a project.

v1ScoreFactor.description:
A score factor for an object. Each score factor
describes a piece of information used while computing the overall score.
Each factor is associated with a specific category. Score factors can have a
positive impact on the repository score and then they have a positive score, or can
have a negative impact on the overall score and then they have a positive score.
The description captures additional information for the particular factor.
In general there are many (tens or hundreds) of such score factors split across the ScoreCategory categories.

Postive score factor example:

 Category: SCORE_CATEGORY_BEST_PRACTICES

 Score: 2

 Description: The repository is enforcing signed commits.

Negative score factor example:

Category: SCORE_CATEGORY_VULNERABILITIES

Score: -1

Description: the repository has unresolved issues related to vulnerabilities that have been open for more than 3 months.

v1SimpleContainerImage.description:
SimpleContainerImage describes the structure of a basic container image signature payload, as defined at:
https://github.com/containers/image/blob/main/docs/containers-signature.5.md#json-data-format.

We don't really need to use these definitions since they are only kept in our database and will
not be visible externally. However, if we ever decide to save our signatures as part of the OCI
container registries or even be asked to "export" our data for customers that perhaps want to
migrate to cosign or notary, then this will make this effort more seamless because it's the
standard format used.

AND'd with the score-predicate branch when both are configured.

score_at_or_below.description:
Match when the overall score is at or below this threshold
(scores are 1-10, higher = safer). OR'd with dimension_at_or_below.

v1SkillActivity.description:
SkillActivity matches skills by name patterns and/or score thresholds.
Match logic: configured branches are AND'd — when both name_matchers
and score predicates are set, both must hold for the match to fire;
when only one is set, only that one must hold; if neither is set,
the activity never matches. Within the score branch, score_at_or_below
and every set field of dimension_at_or_below are OR'd: any single
satisfied threshold fires the branch. When score predicates are set
but no SkillMeta is available for the skill, the score branch is
configured-but-cannot-fire, failing the AND with the name branch
(fail-safe).

v1SkillDimensionThresholds.description:
SkillDimensionThresholds holds per-dimension score thresholds for

Set dimensions are OR'd among themselves and with score_at_or_below:
any single dimension at or below its threshold fires the predicate.
Dimension names mirror AgenticInventory.SkillScoreDimensions.

SystemEvaluationMethodDefinition is the type of evaluation method implemented
by the system.

 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_VULNERABILITIES: VULNERABILITIES calculates vulnerability related findings.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_SCORES: SCORES calculates score related findings.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_CONDITIONS: CONDITIONS calculates findings related to specific conditions.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_POLICIES: POLICIES evaluates methods based on user defined policies.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_TYPOSQUATTING: TYPOSQUATTING calculates the findings related to typosquatted packages.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_CIS: CIS calculates the findings related to CIS benchmark requirements.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_MALWARE: MALWARE calculates the findings related to malware.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_SECURITY_REVIEW: SECURITY REVIEW calculates security review related findings.
 - SYSTEM_EVALUATION_METHOD_DEFINITION_AI_SAST: AI_SAST calculates AI SAST related findings.

 - SYSTEM_ROLE_READ_ONLY: READ_ONLY only can read all data, but perform no updates.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_POLICY_EDITOR: Policy editor has read access on all objects, and the ability to create and
manage policies.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_CODE_SCANNER: CODE_SCANNER has all permissions to run a scan and view the results.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_ENDOR_PATCHING: ENDOR_PATCHING has permissions to use Endor Lab's factory.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_SYNC_ORG: SYNC_ORG has permissions to perform a sync-org scan on all supported
platforms (GitHub, Azure, GitLab etc).
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_ONPREM_SCHEDULER: ONPREM_SCHEDULER has permissions to perform sync-org, scans and manage
onprem scheduler related objects.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_ENDOR_PROXY: Deprecated: Use SYSTEM_ROLE_PACKAGE_FIREWALL instead.
ENDOR_PROXY has permissions to access proxy endpoints in endorfactory service.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_PACKAGE_FIREWALL: PACKAGE_FIREWALL has permissions to access firewall endpoints for package firewall in endorfactory service.
 - SYSTEM_ROLE_AI_AUDIT: AI_AUDIT has least-privilege permissions to run ai-audit hooks (agent session events).

columns.description: The number of columns in the table.

column_ids.description:
A map from a column name to an ID. The IDs in the rows of the
table are used to avoid repeating the column name.

column_types.description: A map from a column ID to a type. This will be used to read the values of the columns in each row.

v1TableHeader.description:
Contains information for the table.
It is repeated in each TableRowGroup even though it contains the same information.

v1TableRow.description: A table row contains a map with the values for each column.

uuid.description: The UUID of the table row group.

tenant_meta.description: TableRowGroups are associated with a tenant and namespace.

v1TableRowGroup.description:
TableRowGroup in the main object that contains an ordered list of TableRows
and TableDescription with general information about the table.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project that to which the TableRowGroup is related.

sequence.description: The sequence number indicates the order of this group among all the groups in the table.

type.description: Target type.

name.description: Target name. Example: linux, dotnet, x86_64.

version.description:
Target version, for example, 6.0.0 for the dotnet framework
version 6.0.0. If there is no version specified for a target then that
means that a dependency is applicable for all versions of that target.
This field is optional because few targets, such as CPU_ARCH,
do not have a version.

exclude.description: Set to true if a dependency is excluded from the target.

v1TaskStatus.description: TaskStatus represents the lifecycle state of an analysis task.

uuid.description: The UUID of the telemetry.

tenant_meta.description: Namespace of the message that is accessed.

v1Telemetry.description: Telemetry represents the Prometheus metrics obtained from endorctl processes.

metric_families.description: An array of metric families sent to the server.

execution_id.description: The UUID for the endorctl run.

caller_prefix.description: Identifies where the metrics come from.

v1TemplateParamName.description:
TemplateParamName is the name of the template param used in secret validation profiles.

 - TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_CLIENT_ID: "ClientID" is the template parameter name for client ID.
 - TEMPLATE_PARAM_NAME_TENANT_ID: "TenantID" is the template parameter name for tenant ID.

uuid.description: The UUID of a tenant.

v1Tenant.description:
Tenant represents a tenant in the system.

Mostly includes tenant configuration parameters.

namespace.description:
Namespaces are a way to organize organizational units into virtual
groupings of resources. Namespaces must be a fully qualified name,
for example, the child namespace of namespace "endor.prod" called "app"
is called "endor.prod.app".

v1TenantMeta.description: Tenant related data for the tenant containing the resource.

street.description: The street address of a user.

city.description: The city of a users address.

state.description: The state of a users address.

organizational_entity_name.title:
The human-readable name of the organization. Will be used as supplier for the SBOM.
Although this is not a required field this will be validated when trying to export an SBOM.bool

organizational_contacts.description: The list of contact that we can put as the contact in the SBOM export supplier information.

organization_urls.description: The list of URLs which are associated with the given organization which can be included in the supplier SBOM information.

placement_zone.description: The placement zone for internal tenant routing and sharding.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp of the slot. The resolution of this timestamp
depends on the time resolution we are tracking, so for
daily resolution will be the 12:00am of the day.

count.description: The count of activity in the slot.

tag_activity.description:
The breakdown of activity per tag. When we track an activity,
it can be associated with a user specified tag (for example, "Open" for a PR).
So here we get the per-tag breakdown.

v1TimeSlot.description:
Structure that contains activity information for a given slot of time.
Each slot could  capture activity for one day, month or year, depending on the resolution used.

v1TimeTracker.description:
Tge sequence of TimeSlots for each time resolution we track.
We can track multiple resolutions, and some resolutions may be empty.

token.description: The opaque token credential; see the message doc for per-ecosystem wire encoding.

v1TokenAuth.description:
TokenAuth is a single opaque token credential. Its wire encoding is
ecosystem-specific (see per-spec doc comments): a literal Authorization:
Bearer header where the tooling supports it (Maven), otherwise the HTTP
Basic password. Named TokenAuth (not BearerAuth) precisely because it is
not a bearer header on every ecosystem.

v1ToolChainProfile.description:
ToolChainProfile represents the list of tool chains that need to be
installed.

name.description: name of the tool chain.

relative_tool_chain_path.description: relative path of the tool chain in tar ball.

urls.description: http mirros from where the tool can be downloaded.

sha256_sum.description: SHA256 Digest of the tool that will be downloaded.

v1ToolChainVersion.description: ToolChainVersion defines the tool chain's source from where it can be installed.

environment_variables.description: environment_variables are the env variables to be set during toolchain installation.

uuid.description: The UUID of the tool pattern.

tenant_meta.description: Rules are associated with a tenant and namespace.

meta.description: Metadata identifies the tool pattern object.

propagate.description: Indicates that the object should be visible in child namespaces.

v1ToolPattern.description: ToolPattern represents the search pattern data for one tool.

categories.description:
List of control function categories (based on static name to category mapping).
Examples: Build, CI/CD Pipeline, Code Coverage, Container Orchestration, Container Registry, Dependency Mgmt, Documentation, IaC, License Mgmt, Linters, Monitoring, Package Mgmt, Publishers, SBOM, SCA, Secrets, Security, Signing and Verification, Testing, VMs, Vulnerability Mgmt.

file_patterns.description:
List of search patterns that are applied file/path names (filename_patterns) and, if present, their content (line_patterns).
Examples:
A file name match for "Dockerfile$" identifies Docker.
A match for line_pattern "\[tool\.black\]" inside a file with a filename_pattern match for "pyproject.toml$" idenfies Python Black.

cmd_patterns.description:
List of search patterns that are applied to the content of all CI/CD pipeline definition files.
Example: "endorctl scan" identifies Endor Labs usage inside tool configuration files that contain shell commands.

tool_patterns.description:
Map of search patterns that are applied to the content of specific tool definition files, indexed by tool name.
Example: ".*uses: sonarsource/sonarcloud-github-action@.*" identifies sonarcloud inside a GitHub Actions file, so it is listed under "ghactions" here.
The index string must match the name of the other tool in order for the infrastructure to cross-reference them.

webhook_patterns.description:
List of search patterns that are applied to webhook payload URLs.
Example: https://coveralls.io/webhook.

badge_patterns.description:
List of badge URL patterns.
Example: codecov.io.

display_name.description:
Display name if different from tool name.
Example: "GitHub Actions" might be the display name for "ghactions".

v1ToolPatternSpec.description: The internal specification of the object.

uuid.description: The UUID of the saved view.

tenant_meta.description: The Tenant Metadata restricts access to a specific tenant.

spec.description:
The specification of the saved view: scope, surface, view type,
optional base reference, query, and display configuration.

propagate.description: Propagate controls the visibility of the saved view in child namespaces.

v1UISavedView.description:
UISavedView persists a view configuration (query values + display
preferences) over an Endor resource.

v1UISavedViewScope.description:
Who owns / can see the view. Determines lookup precedence and sharing.

 - SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED: No scope has been set.
 - SCOPE_PERSONAL: Visible only to the user who created the view.
 - SCOPE_NAMESPACE: Shared with everyone in the owning namespace.

scope.description: Ownership / visibility classification of the view.

owner_claims.title:
Subject claims of the user who created this view. Populated by the
server at create time and immutable thereafter. Used for SCOPE_PERSONAL
visibility filtering. Empty for other types

surface.description:
Surface identifier that scopes the view to a specific UI area, e.g.
"findings.table" or "packages.inventory". Lowercase, dot-separated
segments of [a-z0-9_].

query.description: The query executed to produce the rows for this view.

display.description:
Free-form display configuration (column order, widths, sort, grouping,
etc.). Shape is owned by the frontend and versioned via display_version.

display_version.description:
Schema version of the display payload. Allows the frontend to migrate
older display blobs when the shape evolves.

v1UISavedViewSpec.description: Spec captures the saved view's configuration.

uuid.description: The UUID of the UI telemetry.

tenant_meta.description: Namespace where the telemetry events were recorded.

v1UITelemetry.description: UITelemetry represents events observered from the Endor UI.

user_id.description: The user to which these events belong.

session_id.description: The user session to which these events belong.

events.description: A batched list of events observed from the UI.

device_user_agent.description: Additional browser information from the device sending the events.

device_screen_info.description: Additional screen size information from the device sending the events.

name.description:
Name of the unsupported project, which can be an unsupported clone URL or
a package name.

v1UnsupportedSpec.description: A project with a source code type that is not supported or not known.

update_mask.description: Fields to update. Defaults to all fields.

force.description:
Force will force the update of the resource if any
checks fail.

v1UpdateRequest.description: Message used for all update requests.

uuid.description: The UUID of a user.

v1User.description:
User represents a user in the system.

Mostly includes configuration parameters that are user wise.

v1UserInfoResponse.description: UserInfoResponse returns information about a user and their authentication token.

user_name.title:
Username of a user.
Usernames are automatically derived from the token.
Depending on the identity source it can be the
nickname (GitHub) or email (Google and others)

first_name.description: First name of the user as identified. It can be changed.

last_name.description: Last name of the user. It can be changed.

email.description: Email of the user. It can be changed.

last_login_time.description:
Last login time keeps a record of the last time
that the user logged in.

event_tracking.description: Lists of user events indexed by event type.

token_hash.description:
The hash of the last token issued to the user.
During authentication we make sure that this hash matches
the token provided.

groups.description:
Groups that the user is a member of, as identified by the
claims returned by the identity provider.

uuid.description: The UUID of the user telemetry.

tenant_meta.description: Namespace where the telemetry events were recorded.

v1UserTelemetry.description: UserTelemetry represents user-specific events observered from the Endor Labs UI.

user_id.description: The user to which these events belong.

session_id.description: The user session to which these events belong.

event_store.description: Lists of user events indexed by event type.

kind.description:
Identifies the specification the output conforms to. VEX is emitted as
CycloneDx, so only CycloneDx (1) is accepted.

format.description:
Serialization format of the rendered VEX document. Restricted to JSON (1)
and XML (2).

component_type.description: Library or application classification for the VEX root component.

include_test_dependencies.description:
Whether to include findings against test/dev/build/optional dependencies.
When false (default), findings whose target dependency is non-production —
or only reachable from the root through non-production paths — are excluded.

export_parameters.description:
Parameters describing which package versions to include in the VEX.
Supports project_uuid / project_name / package_version_uuids variants.

package_version_uuid.description:
UUID of a single PackageVersion to export. When set, the handler generates
a VEX containing just this package version's findings. Mutually exclusive
with export_parameters.

cyclonedx_spec_version.description:
CycloneDx specification version the rendered document conforms to. VEX is
emitted as CycloneDx, so an SPDX version is not representable here. Leave
unset to take the CycloneDx default of 1.5.

v1VEXExportJobRequest.description: Request holds the input parameters for running a VEX export job.

file_path.description:
The file path of the generated VEX document in object storage.
Stored on the Job by the handler; the apiserver Job RPC layer reads this
on every GetJob and produces a fresh signed download URL.

report_url.description:
The signed download URL for the generated VEX document. Populated by the
apiserver Job RPC layer on each GetJob call (5-minute TTL).

vex_size_bytes.description:
Byte length of the generated VEX artifact in object storage. Useful for
clients deciding whether to show a download progress indicator and for
operational reporting on export sizes.

resource_namespace.description:
Namespace jobctl read the referenced resources from — the caller's
tenant, or "oss" if the fallback fired.

v1VEXExportJobResponse.description: Response holds the output after the VEX export job completes.

key.description: The unique identifier of the API key.

secret.description: The secret associated with the provided API Key.

valid.description: Valid returns if the API key and secret pair are valid.

issuing_user.description: The user that creates the API key.

v1ValidationStatus.description:
Status of secret validation.

 - VALIDATION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: No validator.
 - VALIDATION_STATUS_FAILURE: Failed to validate secret.
 - VALIDATION_STATUS_SECRET_IS_VALID: Secret is valid.
 - VALIDATION_STATUS_SECRET_IS_INVALID: Secret is invalid

vulnerable_component_resource_id.description: The Resource ID of the vulnerable component created in Vanta.

package_vulnerability_resource_id.description: The Resource ID of the package vulnerability created in Vanta.

sca_resource_id.description: The Resource ID of the static code analysis vulnerabilities created in Vanta.

uuid.description: The UUID of an VectorStore.

tenant_meta.description: VectorStores are associated with a tenant or are global.

spec.description: The internal specification of the object.

propagate.description: Vector stores can be propagated and accessed in child namespaces.

v1VectorStore.description:
Represents a vector store in the system. The vector store will create all
the infrastructure for semantic searches.

v1VectorStoreData.description:
VectorStoreData is the message for uploading data to the vector store.
It allows batch uploads.

v1VectorStoreDataDeleteQuery.description:
VectorStoreDataDeleteQuery deletes documents matching filter whose uniqueness
field values are NOT in the provided retain set. This is a generic "prune" operation
useful for incremental index refresh.

request.description: Request contains the input parameters for the delete operation.

response.description: Response contains the output from the delete operation.

v1VectorStoreDataDeleteQuerySpec.description: Spec is the specification of the delete request.

vector_store_uuid.description: vector_store_uuid is the ID of the vector store to delete data from.

filter.description:
filter scopes the deletion to documents matching this filter.
e.g., {"repo": "/path/to/repo"} to only affect documents from a specific repo.

keep_filters.description:
keep_filters contains the filters to keep.
Each entry is a Struct with field values matching the vector store's fields.
e.g., {"fqn": "com.example.Foo.bar", "repo": "/path/to/repo"} to keep documents from a specific repo and fqn.

v1VectorStoreDataDeleteQuerySpecRequest.description: Request contains the input parameters for the delete operation.

deleted_count.description: deleted_count is the number of documents that were deleted.

v1VectorStoreDataDeleteQuerySpecResponse.description: Response contains the output from the delete operation.

v1VectorStoreDataDocumentConsistencyQuer.description:
VectorStoreDataDocumentConsistencyQuery checks which documents need to be updated in a vector store.
This is a lightweight check that only requires uniqueness fields and content hash,
avoiding the need to send full document content over the wire.

request.description: Request contains the input parameters for the needs update check.

response.description: Response contains the results of the needs update check.

v1VectorStoreDataDocumentConsistencyQuer.description: Spec is the specification of the needs update query.

vector_store_uuid.description: vector_store_uuid is the ID of the vector store to check against.

documents.description: documents contains the lightweight document check requests.

v1VectorStoreDataDocumentConsistencyQuer.description: Request contains the input parameters for the needs update check.

results.description: results contains the consistency results, in the same order as the request documents.

v1VectorStoreDataDocumentConsistencyQuer.description: Response contains the results of the entry match check.

v1VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQuery.description:
VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQuery patches the metadata of stored documents
without touching their content or embeddings.

Re-uploading a document cannot do this: the upload path skips any document
whose uniqueness key and content hash already match what is stored, so a
metadata-only change is silently dropped. Deleting and re-adding would work
but re-embeds every document and leaves a window where the document is
missing, which for summary stores means an interrupted run re-pays the LLM
that produced it. This applies the patch in place instead.

request.description: Request contains the input parameters for the metadata update operation.

response.description: Response contains the output from the metadata update operation.

v1VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQuerySpec.description: Spec is the specification of the metadata update request.

vector_store_uuid.description: vector_store_uuid is the ID of the vector store holding the documents.

filter.description:
filter selects the documents to patch, e.g.
{"repo": "/path/to/repo", "file_path": "src/a.go"}.
Required and must be non-empty: an empty filter would rewrite every
document in the store.

metadata.description:
metadata holds the keys to set on each matching document. Keys absent
from this struct are left as they are, so this is a patch rather than a
replacement, and re-running the same request is a no-op.

v1VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQuerySpec.description: Request contains the input parameters for the metadata update operation.

updated_count.description: updated_count is the number of documents that were patched.

v1VectorStoreDataMetadataUpdateQuerySpec.description: Response contains the output from the metadata update operation.

vector_store_uuid.description: vector_store_uuid is the ID of the vector store to upload data.

documents.description: data is the data to upload to the vector store.

data.description: data is the data to upload to the vector store.

metadata.description: metadata is the metadata of the document.

score.description: score is the score of the document.

save_content.description: save_content controls whether document content is saved to the store.

content_hash.description: content_hash is the SHA256 hash of the document content.

v1VectorStoreDocument.description: VectorStoreDocument is the standard format of documents in the vector store.

v1VectorStoreMetadataQuery.description: VectorStoreMetadataQuery is the message to query the vector store by metadata.

request.description: Request contains the input parameters for the metadata query operation.

response.description: Response contains the output from the metadata query operation.

v1VectorStoreMetadataQuerySpec.description: Spec is the specification of the metadata query request.

vector_store_uuid.description: vector_store_uuid is the ID of the vector store to query.

filter.description: filter is the metadata filter to search for matching documents.

v1VectorStoreMetadataQuerySpecRequest.description: Request contains the input parameters for the metadata query operation.

matches.description: matches contains the documents matching the metadata filter.

v1VectorStoreMetadataQuerySpecResponse.description: Response contains the output from the metadata query operation.

v1VectorStoreQuery.description: VectorStoreQuery is the message to query the vector store.

vector_store_uuid.description: vector_store_uuid is the ID of the vector store to upload data.

query.description: query is the actual query string.

matches.description: data is the data to upload to the vector store.

metadata_filter.title: metadata_filter is an optional filter to scope the similarity search to documents

embedding_provider.description: EmbeddingProvider is the embedding provider of the vector store.

embedding_model.description: EmbeddingModel is the embedding model of the vector store.

dimensions.description: Dimensions is the number of dimensions to be used.

uniqueness_fields.description:
uniqueness_fields specifies which metadata fields are used for document uniqueness.
When provided, a unique index is created on these fields at store creation time.
All add/update/delete operations must include these fields in document metadata.

apply_uniqueness_index_changes.description:
apply_uniqueness_index_changes explicitly authorizes migrating uniqueness indexes
when the requested uniqueness_fields differ from the currently provisioned index.
This must be true any time changes are made to the uniqueness_fields.

search_index_fields.description:
search_index_fields lists metadata fields that queries filter on beyond the
uniqueness fields. A non-unique index is ensured on each field when the store
is created or next opened, so equality filters on it can avoid a full scan.
The declared set is authoritative: adding a field creates its index and
removing a field drops it, both on the next open.

sha.description:
SHA of the source control version.
Because the SHA might not be possible to resolved this field is optional.

ref.description:
Resolved ref of the source control version.
Can be a tag, a branch or a SHA.

uuid.description: The UUID of the version diff.

tenant_meta.description: Tenant metadata information.

spec.description: The internal specification of the object.

v1VersionUpgrade.description:
VersionUpgrade contains all information about a possible version upgrade of a dependency package.
This upgrade object can be under a project or a package version object.

project_uuid.description: The UUID of the project to which this version upgrade relates.

upgrade_info.description: Information for a single version upgrade.

name.description: The name of the project or package version for this record.

configuration.description: Configuration that was used in the computation.

uuid.description: The UUID of a vulnerability.

v1Vuln.description: Vuln represents an Endor Labs vulnerability in the system.

deepdive.description:
Indicates whether the research team performed full analysis on multiple
artifact_ids involved in CVE.

disputed.description:
Indicates whether the research team considers a CVE should be disputed
based on analysis.

additional_notes.description: Notes by the person that processed the CVE.

published.description: The RFC3339 timestamp indicating when this entry was published.

modified.description: The RFC3339 timestamp indicating when this entry was last modified.

withdrawn.description:
Optional. The RFC3339 timestamp indicating when this entry is considered
to be withdrawn.

aliases.description: Optional. IDs for the same vulnerability in other databases.

related.description:
Optional. List of IDs of closely related vulnerabilities, such as the
same problem in alternate ecosystems.

cvss_v4_severity.description: Optional. CVSS v4.0 severity of the vulnerability.

database_specific.description:
Optional. JSON object holding additional information about the
vulnerability as defined by the database for which the record applies.

malicious.description: Indicates whether this item is classified as malicious or not.

additional_endor_notes.description: Notes from the Endor Labs analysis of the vulnerability.

vulnerabilities.description: A list of all the vulnerabilities found affecting this package or package version.

v1VulnerabilityStats.description: VulnerabilityFactors message includes all vulnerability related data.

custom_headers.description:
Additional HTTP headers attached to every webhook request, evaluated
independently of auth_method. Enables forwarding to systems that
require non-Bearer auth headers (Datadog, Splunk, New Relic, Elastic).

open_action_template.description: The template to be used for OPEN action for webhook plugin.

update_action_template.description: The template to be used for UPDATE action for webhook plugin.

resolve_action_template.description: The template to be used for RESOLVE action for webhook plugin.
